# Keto meals & smoothies recipe library

140 keto recipes, including household recipes and adaptations from linked publishers. Ingredient quantities use four portions; whole-bird recipes round up to complete batches. Every base meal serving or estimated 8 fl oz smoothie glass has no more than 12.5 g net carbs. Each recipe includes shared-table serving ideas. Optional measured per-person sides default to none and their nutrition is separate. Adaptations have not been kitchen-tested.

## Lemon salmon and asparagus

4 adult servings · US imperial measures · keto · 8 min active per base batch · 25 min

Lemon salmon with asparagus and garlic.

No mid-cook action; remove fish and asparagus separately at their endpoints.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

Then: Asparagus basket: spread without a dense pile; air fry at 390°F for 7–10 min, check at 7 min; remove when ready.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.48 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Half to asparagus; half to salmon.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> Garlic powder<small class="trn-state-detail">Divide equally.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the proportional split described in the method.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.06 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.71 oz</strong> Hemp hearts<small class="trn-state-detail">hulled · Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Skin-on salmon fillets — raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick. Choose individual fillets about 6 oz each, keeping the stated thickness.

- 1 lb Asparagus — trimmed, medium stalks

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half to asparagus; half to salmon.

- 1 tsp Garlic powder. Divide equally.

- ½ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 0.07 oz Lemon zest — finely grated. Use finely grated zest.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.71 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

### Equipment

- Two air fryers with room for four fillets in one basket and 454 g asparagus in the other

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Preheat both fryers to 390°F. Toss asparagus with half the oil, half the garlic, and half the salt. Spread in one basket without a dense pile.

2. **Cook.** Pat salmon dry. Rub with remaining oil, garlic, salt, pepper, and zest. Put skin-side down in the other basket with gaps between fillets. Start both together.

3. **Finish.** Check asparagus at 7 minutes; medium stalks usually need 7–10. Check salmon at 10 minutes; allow 10–14 to reach 145°F. Remove each when ready. Finish with lemon juice and hemp.

### For a shared table

Serve the salmon and asparagus as written. Offer cooked rice in a separate bowl for diners who want a starch.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 6–8 min. Toss and load separate baskets; preheat overlaps prep.

- Air fry together: 7–14 min. Check asparagus at 7 min and salmon at 10 min; remove each separately.

- Finish: 2 min. Check fish at 145°F; add lemon and hemp.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Lemon brightens the salmon; hemp adds a mild nutty finish without another cooking step.

- Thin asparagus needs an earlier check.

- Keep the fillets skin-side down and apart.

If either basket cannot hold its full batch, use two half-sheet pans at 425°F: fish about 12–18 min, asparagus 10–15 min; allow 25–35 min total.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 468 kcal; protein: 39.0 g; fat: 32.2 g; total carbs: 6.1 g; fiber: 2.8 g; net carbs: 3.3 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: fish. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Basket fit and actual thickness can change the time; first cook has not been kitchen-tested.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

## Smoky chicken thighs and broccoli

4 adult servings · US imperial measures · keto · 12 min active per base batch · 35 min

Smoky chicken thighs with roasted broccoli.

Start broccoli five minutes after chicken; shake broccoli once.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

### Cooking flow (Tabular Recipe Notation)

Start chicken first; start broccoli 5 min later.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4" class="trn-prep">Use uncrowded baskets; thighs must be unfolded and no more than ¾ inch thick.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4" class="trn-prep">If smaller baskets cannot hold the batch uncrowded, use extra batches or the oven fallback.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.5 lb</strong> Boneless skinless chicken thighs<small class="trn-state-essential">raw, thawed, unfolded; no more than ¾ inch thick</small></th><td rowspan="7" colspan="2" class="trn-operation">Coat unfolded thighs with oil, paprika, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Then: Broccoli basket: start 5 min after chicken; air fry at 390°F for 10–14 min, shake once halfway; stems fork-tender, crowns lightly browned.</td><td rowspan="5" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Finish cooked broccoli with lemon juice and nutritional yeast.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.48 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Half to broccoli; half to chicken.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the proportional split described in the method.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.53 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.28 oz</strong> Nutritional yeast<small class="trn-state-detail">flakes · Add after cooking.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, unfolded; no more than ¾ inch thick

- 1 lb Broccoli florets — about 1½ inches across

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half to broccoli; half to chicken.

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Dried oregano

- ¾ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.28 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Add after cooking.

### Equipment

- Two air fryers with uncrowded baskets

- Instant-read thermometer

- Separate raw-poultry bowl and clean serving tools

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Preheat both fryers to 390°F. Toss broccoli with half the oil and one third of the salt; load one basket without crowding. In a separate bowl coat chicken with the remaining oil and salt, paprika, garlic, oregano, and pepper.

2. **Cook.** Put unfolded thighs smooth-side up in the other basket without overlapping. Start chicken. Five minutes later, start broccoli.

3. **Finish.** Shake broccoli once halfway through its 10–14-minute cook. Chicken usually needs 16–22 minutes; check the thickest pieces for 165°F. No chicken flip is required, though the underside browns less. Finish broccoli with lemon and nutritional yeast. Broccoli is ready when stems are fork-tender and crowns are lightly browned; time alone is not its endpoint.

### For a shared table

Plate the smoky chicken and broccoli for everyone, with baked potatoes served separately. Keep the lemon and nutritional yeast on the broccoli.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load chicken: 7–9 min. Start chicken first; preheat overlaps prep.

- Start broccoli: 5 min after chicken. Load broccoli basket.

- Cook: Chicken 16–22 min; broccoli 10–14 min. Shake broccoli once halfway; check chicken thickest pieces for 165°F.

- Finish: 2 min. Add lemon and yeast after cooking.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Smoked paprika and oregano season the thighs while lemon and yeast sharpen the broccoli after cooking.

- Chicken underside browns less without a flip.

- Keep yeast out of the fryer to avoid scorching.

If baskets cannot hold the batch, use two oven pans at 425°F for about 20–25 min; allow 35–40 min total and check chicken for 165°F.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 317 kcal; protein: 37.9 g; fat: 14.3 g; total carbs: 9.6 g; fiber: 3.8 g; net carbs: 5.8 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: none listed; check every product label. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Smaller fryer baskets require the oven fallback or extra batches.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

## Pesto cod and zucchini

4 adult servings · US imperial measures · keto · 11 min active per base batch · 40 min

Pesto cod with zucchini.

One scheduled fish-pan addition, then separate vegetable/fish endpoint checks.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

### Cooking flow (Tabular Recipe Notation)

<div class="trn-scroll" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Pesto cod and zucchini cooking flow, scroll horizontally"><table class="trn-table"><tbody><tr><td colspan="4" class="trn-prep">Heat oven to 425°F on bake. Use two separate 18×13-inch rimmed metal half-sheet pans.</td></tr><tr><td colspan="4" class="trn-prep">Start zucchini first; add fish pan 6 min later. Remove each pan at its own endpoint and serve promptly.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.5 lb</strong> Cod fillets<small class="trn-state-essential">raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick · Choose individual fillets about 6 oz each, keeping the stated thickness.</small></th><td rowspan="2" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Pat thawed, 1-inch-thick cod dry; rub with oil and place on its own pan. Then: Fish pan: add 6 min after zucchini; roast at 425°F for 12–18 min, check at 12 min of fish cooking; reach 145°F.</td><td rowspan="3" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Spoon pesto over cooked fish after roasting.</td><td rowspan="9" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Plate pesto-topped cod and zucchini separately; finish both with lemon juice and hemp.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.24 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Three quarters to zucchini; remainder to fish.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.59 oz</strong> DeLallo basil pesto<small class="trn-state-essential">squeeze-bottle, as sold · Substitute at most 2 g net carbs per 30 g.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.5 lb</strong> Zucchini<small class="trn-state-detail">sliced into ½-inch half-moons</small></th><td rowspan="4" colspan="2" class="trn-operation">Toss ½-inch zucchini half-moons with oil, salt and pepper; spread on separate pan. Then: Zucchini pan: roast at 425°F for 18–23 min; check at 18 min of zucchini cooking; browned edges and tender center.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.71 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Three quarters to zucchini; remainder to fish.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the measured salt in the zucchini seasoning.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Black pepper<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.53 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.71 oz</strong> Hemp hearts<small class="trn-state-detail">hulled · Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Cod fillets — raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick. Choose individual fillets about 6 oz each, keeping the stated thickness.

- 1.5 lb Zucchini — sliced into ½-inch half-moons

- 1.59 oz DeLallo basil pesto — squeeze-bottle, as sold. Substitute at most 2 g net carbs per 30 g.

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Three quarters to zucchini; remainder to fish.

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the measured salt in the zucchini seasoning.

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.71 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch rimmed metal half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss zucchini with three quarters of the oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on one half-sheet pan. Pat fish dry, rub with the remaining oil, and place on the other pan.

2. **Cook.** Start the zucchini pan first. After 6 minutes, add the fish pan. Check zucchini from 18 minutes of its own cooking time for browned edges and a tender center; allow about 18–23 minutes. Check fish after 12 minutes of its own cooking time; allow about 12–18 minutes to reach 145°F. Remove each pan at its endpoint and serve promptly. If either needs longer, keep checking; do not overcook the fish to match the vegetables.

3. **Finish.** Spoon pesto over cooked fish. Finish fish and zucchini with lemon and hemp. Applying pesto after cooking keeps its basil flavor and avoids burning the sauce.

### For a shared table

Serve the pesto cod and zucchini as written, with separately cooked pasta available for other plates. Keep the measured pesto on the fish rather than stretching it through the pasta.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load zucchini: 10–12 min. Preheat overlaps prep; fish and zucchini get separate pans.

- Give zucchini a head start: 6 min. Add fish pan after 6 minutes: one scheduled main-appliance action.

- Finish both pans: Fish 12–18 min; zucchini 18–23 min total roast. Check zucchini for browned edges and tenderness; fish must reach 145°F. Remove separately at their endpoints.

- Finish: 2 min. Spoon pesto on fish; add lemon and hemp and serve promptly.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Separating wet zucchini keeps cod from steaming in vegetable liquid; pesto stays fresh when added after heat.

- The six-minute vegetable head start reduces the fish holding time; doneness still decides when each pan comes out.

- Pesto goes on after cooking to protect basil flavor.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 328 kcal; protein: 33.9 g; fat: 15.7 g; total carbs: 7.2 g; fiber: 2.3 g; net carbs: 4.9 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: fish, milk, tree-nuts. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Pesto substitution needs no more than 2 g net carbs per 30 g to preserve the keto estimate.

- Two-pans and conventional bake are assumed.

- Pesto may contain tree nuts or other allergens; verify the specific jar label. This data is not an allergy guarantee.

- The six-minute head start is a design adjustment, not a tested synchronization guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 12 count Large eggs — as purchased

- 2.67 fl oz Water — potable. Mix into the eggs.

- 1 lb Frozen chopped spinach — package weight before thawing and squeezing. Heat according to package directions, cool until safe to handle and press very dry in a sieve. · Buy 1 × 16 oz (454 g) packages; measure out the required weight.

- 2.65 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

- 1.41 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

- 0.28 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Mix into eggs.

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the measured salt in the egg mixture; feta adds salt too.

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 0.63 oz Olive oil — as purchased. One quarter for the dish; three quarters for the salad.

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

### Equipment

- Oven at 375°F on bake

- Microwave for spinach

- 9-inch square metal baking dish at least 2 inches deep

- Instant-read thermometer

- Scaling: at six or eight servings use two matching 9-inch square metal dishes, dividing the mixture to preserve original depth; oven loading can increase total time. At two servings the thinner layer may finish earlier; check the center without blindly halving the timer.

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 375°F. Heat spinach in the microwave according to its package during preheating, then let it cool until safe to handle and press very dry in a fine-mesh sieve with a spoon. Do not squeeze hot spinach with bare hands. Use one quarter of the oil to grease one 9-inch square metal dish for two or four servings, or two matching dishes for six or eight; each must be at least 2 inches deep.

2. **Cook.** Whisk eggs, water, garlic, salt, and pepper. Stir in squeezed spinach, feta, hemp, and yeast. Divide between the selected dishes so the mixture is no deeper than the original four-serving layer.

3. **Finish.** For the original four-serving layer, bake about 25–30 minutes; for the thinner two-serving layer, begin checking at 18 minutes, until the center is set and reaches 160°F. Toss greens with the remaining oil and lemon during baking. Rest the frittata for 3 minutes before cutting into the selected number of equal adult portions.

### For a shared table

Keep the full egg, feta and hemp frittata with its salad. Offer toast alongside individual non-keto plates.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat, thaw, and mix: 12–15 min. Microwave spinach per package, cool enough to handle and press dry while preheating; oil dish and whisk mixture. Cooling or thawing delays can add time.

- Bake: 25–30 min. No mid-cook action; make salad during bake. Check center for 160°F.

- Rest and serve: 3 min. Cut into the selected number of equal adult portions.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Dry spinach prevents a watery center; feta, hemp, and yeast add savory depth.

- Squeezing spinach very dry matters more than extending the bake.

- Package spinach weight is before squeezing; drained nutrient retention is uncertain.

- Feta can use animal rennet. For a vegetarian version, check for vegetarian or microbial rennet; the generic cheese label is not verified here.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 408 kcal; protein: 30.3 g; fat: 28.4 g; total carbs: 10.0 g; fiber: 5.0 g; net carbs: 5.0 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: egg, milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Actual spinach drain and center cook time need a first cook.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

- Allow 40–50 minutes; safe spinach handling, thawing and pressing can extend prep. Two servings bake in a thinner layer: start checking the center at 18 minutes rather than assuming the four-serving time.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

Sauté first, then quick release after 5 minutes; stir in cream and kale.

### Ingredients

- 6.42 oz Chicken Italian sausage — raw, casings removed. No pork; check the label for allergens and fillers.

- 2.36 oz Turkey bacon — chopped

- 0.78 oz Onion — diced

- 0.02 oz Crushed red pepper — flakes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.14 oz Garlic — minced

- 26.04 fl oz Chicken broth or 26.04 fl oz Water — thin, water-based

- 6.03 oz Cauliflower florets — bite-size

- 3.35 oz Organic heavy cream — added after pressure cooking

- 1.48 oz Kale — stems removed, chopped. Kale, not spinach.

- 0.03 oz Xanthan gum

- 0.35 oz Parmesan — grated

### Equipment

- Instant Pot 6QT or larger

- Instant-read thermometer

- Ladle

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Dice the onion, mince the garlic, chop the turkey bacon and kale, and cut cauliflower into bite-size florets. Remove sausage casings. Keep raw sausage, its board and utensils away from the kale and cream.

2. **Sauté.** Set the Instant Pot to Sauté. Brown the sausage, breaking it up, with the turkey bacon. Add the onion and crushed red pepper and cook until the onion softens. Add the garlic for about 30 seconds. Turn Sauté off.

3. **Cook.** Add the broth and scrape up browned bits so the pot does not trigger a burn warning. Add the cauliflower. Seal, switch Keep Warm off, and cook at high pressure for 5 minutes. Stay under PC MAX.

4. **Finish.** Quick release according to your manual, keeping clear of steam; vent in short bursts if the soup sputters. Open only after the float valve drops. Check the sausage reaches 165°F. Stir in the cream and kale until the kale wilts. Sprinkle in xanthan while stirring if you want a thicker soup. Serve with Parmesan if using.

### For a shared table

Keep cauliflower in the shared soup. Offer cooked potato pieces in a separate bowl to add only after each keto bowl has been served.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare and sauté: about 12 min. Brown sausage and turkey bacon, then onion, red pepper and garlic.

- Pressurize: 10–15 min expected. Deglaze with broth before sealing; Keep Warm off.

- Pressure cook: 5 min high pressure. Countdown starts after pressure is reached.

- Release and finish: about 5 min. Quick release, open after the float drops, then stir in cream and kale.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Chicken sausage and turkey bacon replace pork, and cauliflower stands in for potatoes to keep the soup keto.

- Deglaze thoroughly after sautéing to avoid a burn warning.

- Add cream only after pressure cooking.

- Kale wilts in the hot soup; no extra cooking needed.

- Xanthan thickens quickly; sprinkle it in while stirring to avoid clumps.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 232 kcal; protein: 13.5 g; fat: 16.8 g; total carbs: 8.0 g; fiber: 1.8 g; net carbs: 6.1 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- 35–45 min is a planning estimate; pressure build time varies with liquid volume and starting temperature.

- Follow your exact model’s liquid minimum, PC MAX, venting and float-valve instructions. Do not leave the operating cooker unattended.

- Nutrition uses USDA smoked Italian turkey sausage as the closest poultry Italian sausage profile, excluding its outlier iron value; check your sausage, bacon and broth labels.

- Household version scaled from a 10-serving batch; not kitchen-tested at other serving counts.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, cut into 1-inch pieces

- 1 lb Cauliflower florets — about 1 inch across

- 0.95 oz Olive oil

- 0.15 oz Ground cumin

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Ground turmeric

- ¼ tsp Ground cinnamon

- ¾ tsp Fine salt

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 4.23 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 5.29 oz Cucumber — diced

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat

### Optional side choices (per diner)

- Cooked rice: 2.82 oz Cooked rice — fully cooked, ready to heat. Heat ready-cooked rice.

- Pita: 2.12 oz Pita — ready to eat; warm briefly. One ready-to-eat 2.12 oz pita per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

- Microwave for ready-to-eat family rice or briefly warmed pita, if serving non-keto diners

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Prepare cucumber and greens. Mix yogurt with its garlic, a pinch of salt and half the lemon juice. Toss cauliflower and chicken with their own oil and spice portions and half the remaining salt on separate 18×13-inch pans.

2. **Cook.** Roast for 18–23 minutes, checking the largest chicken pieces for 165°F and cauliflower for tenderness. If your oven browns unevenly, swap racks halfway.

3. **Finish.** Near the end of roasting, if serving non-keto diners, microwave ready-to-eat rice or briefly warm the chosen pita according to its package. Assemble greens, cucumber, chicken and cauliflower. Add the prepared yogurt sauce and remaining lemon. Put starch on family plates only.

### For a shared table

Set out chicken, cauliflower, cucumber, greens and the full yogurt sauce for everyone. Add the existing cooked-rice or pita option only to the diners who choose it.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 10–12 min. Prepare cold sides and seasoned yogurt sauce first; split remaining spice oil between cauliflower and chicken.

- Roast: 18–23 min. Check largest chicken pieces for 165°F and cauliflower for browned edges and tenderness; optional rack swap if browning unevenly. Heat ready family starch near serving.

- Finish: 2 min. Assemble with prepared yogurt sauce and remaining lemon; starch on family plates only.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Warm spices coat small chicken pieces and cauliflower; cold lemon yogurt balances them.

- Cut chicken into 1-inch pieces; no marinade wait.

- Keep ready-to-eat greens away from raw-poultry tools.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed; strips about 1 inch wide, no more than ¾ inch thick

- 10.58 oz Bell pepper — sliced into ¼-inch strips

- 2.12 oz Onion — sliced into ¼-inch strips

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half of spiced oil on vegetables; half on chicken.

- 2 tsp Mild chili powder blend. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.07 oz Ground cumin

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- 1.06 oz Lime juice — unsweetened

- 5.01 oz Shredded lettuce — washed, ready to eat

- 5.29 oz Avocado flesh — sliced; flesh weight

- 2.12 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

### Optional side choices (per diner)

- Corn tortillas: 1.76 oz Corn tortillas — ready to eat; warm according to package. Two 6-inch tortillas totaling about 1.76 oz per non-keto diner; check the package for wheat or gluten cross-contact. Serve alongside the bowl or fill with part of the filling; two small tortillas will not hold the whole meal.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

- Microwave for family tortillas

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Prepare lettuce and avocado first. Mix oil, spices, and salt. Toss peppers and onion with half the mixture. Coat chicken separately with the rest.

2. **Cook.** Divide chicken and vegetables between two half-sheet pans in a single layer, keeping pieces apart. Bake about 18–22 minutes, until the largest chicken strips reach 165°F. No stir is needed if there is enough space; swap racks halfway if needed for your oven.

3. **Finish.** Finish with lime. Make keto bowls with lettuce, filling, avocado, and yogurt. Near the end of cooking, if serving non-keto diners, heat tortillas in the microwave according to their package for family portions; keep them wrapped until serving. Serve the measured two tortillas alongside each family bowl or fill them with part of the mixture; the full bowl portion is larger than two small tacos.

### For a shared table

Build the keto plates as lettuce bowls with the chicken, avocado and yogurt. Offer the existing two corn tortillas per non-keto diner alongside, or fill them with part of that diner's bowl.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 10–12 min. Prepare lettuce and avocado before raw poultry; separate chicken and vegetables on pans.

- Roast: 18–22 min. Check largest chicken strips for 165°F; swap racks if needed. Heat tortillas during cook.

- Finish: 2 min. Add lime; assemble measured keto bowls and separate family tortillas.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Roasting spaced strips concentrates pepper flavor; lime, avocado, and yogurt round out the bowl.

- Measured peppers, onion, avocado, and yogurt preserve the stated keto nutrition.

- Keep pieces separate so they roast rather than steam.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 378 kcal; protein: 37.5 g; fat: 20.3 g; total carbs: 13.0 g; fiber: 5.9 g; net carbs: 7.1 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Chili powder blends vary by brand and allergen label; inspect package.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

## Salsa verde shredded chicken

4 adult servings · US imperial measures · keto · 15 min active per base batch · 45 min

Salsa verde chicken with avocado and cabbage slaw.

Controlled pressure release, safety check, and shredding at the end; time has a long tail.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

flesh weight</small></th><td rowspan="1" colspan="2" class="trn-operation">Slice avocado.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, separated and unfolded

- 12.68 fl oz Low-sodium chicken broth — thin, water-based. 375 mL base minimum for Instant Pot Duo 6QT; use your model’s minimum.

- 4.37 oz Herdez mild salsa verde — jarred, added after cooking. Substitute at most 2 g total carbs per 31 g; add only after pressure cooking.

- 0.07 oz Ground cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- 1.06 oz Lime juice — unsweetened

- 1 lb Shredded cabbage — plain, no carrots or dressing

- 5.29 oz Avocado flesh — diced; flesh weight

- 2.12 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

### Optional side choices (per diner)

- Cooked rice: 2.82 oz Cooked rice — fully cooked, ready to heat. Heat ready-cooked rice.

### Equipment

- Instant Pot Duo 6QT covered by Duo V5 manual

- Clean board and shredding forks

- Instant-read thermometer

- Microwave for ready-to-eat family rice, if serving non-keto diners

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Put the broth, cumin, garlic, and separated thighs in the Duo 6QT. Leave salsa out. Seal, switch Keep Warm off, and set high pressure for 8 minutes. The broth amount is the 6QT minimum; follow your model’s higher minimum if required and stay under PC MAX.

2. **Cook.** During pressurization, prepare avocado and mix cabbage with yogurt and half the lime. If serving non-keto diners, leave ready-to-eat family rice for microwave heating near serving, according to its package. Keep cold sides away from raw-poultry equipment.

3. **Finish.** When pressure cooking ends, leave the valve at Seal for 10 minutes. Then vent according to your manual, keeping clear of steam. Open only after the float valve drops. Check the thickest thighs for 165°F. If needed, finish cooking in the liquid and recheck; that adds time.

4. **Serve.** Lift onto a clean board and shred. If safely cooked thighs resist shredding, slice or chop them rather than forcing a longer cook for texture alone. Mix with salsa, remaining lime, and only enough broth to moisten. Divide over slaw with avocado. Near serving, if needed, microwave family rice per package and add only to family bowls. Reserve excess broth; no reduction is required.

### For a shared table

Serve salsa verde chicken over the cabbage slaw with avocado. Add the existing cooked-rice option only to individual non-keto bowls.

### Attention timeline

- Load and pressurize: 3 min load + 10–15 min expected pressure build. Broth, spices, thighs only; seal and turn Keep Warm off. Make slaw during build; heat ready family rice near serving.

- Pressure cook: 8 min high pressure. Countdown starts after pressure is reached.

- Release: 10 min natural + about 2 min controlled vent/check. Leave sealed for 10 min; vent per manual, open only after float drops. Probe thighs for 165°F.

- Shred and plate: about 6 min. Shred on clean board, or slice safely cooked thighs if resistant; mix salsa, lime and only enough broth to moisten. Heat ready family rice near serving.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Salsa after pressure cooking keeps its tang and meets the cooker’s need for thin liquid during pressure buildup.

- Keep salsa out of the pressure phase so the thin broth meets the cooker minimum.

- Keep raw-poultry gear away from cold slaw.

- Reserve excess broth; no reduction needed.

- The slaw is lightly dressed rather than creamy. Toss thoroughly and allow it to sit during cooking; check the first-cook texture before changing yogurt or lime amounts.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 327 kcal; protein: 38.6 g; fat: 13.3 g; total carbs: 13.9 g; fiber: 5.5 g; net carbs: 8.4 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- 40–45 min is an expected planning estimate, not a hard bound. The manual permits pressure building up to 30 min, which can make the same meal about 59 min.

- Follow your exact model’s liquid minimum, PC MAX, venting, and float-valve instructions. Do not leave the operating cooker unattended.

- Custom 8+10 timing and shreddability need a first cook.

- Check chicken broth and salsa labels for allergens; the listed milk allergen comes from yogurt. This data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb 93%-lean ground turkey — raw

- 1 count Large egg — as purchased. For fractional eggs, beat whole eggs and weigh 1.76 oz per large-egg portion; half an egg is about 0.88 oz.

- 0.49 oz Ground flaxseed — ground, not whole. Ground seed acts as a binder; whole seeds are not equivalent.

- 1.76 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

- 1 tsp Dried oregano

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 0.16 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Lightly oil baskets.

- 10.58 oz Cucumber — diced

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat

- 4.23 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 3.53 oz.

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

### Optional side choices (per diner)

- Pita: 2.12 oz Pita — ready to eat; warm briefly. One ready-to-eat 2.12 oz pita per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. Serve pita alongside both patties and salad.

- Bun: 1.59 oz Bun — ready to eat; warm briefly. One 1.59 oz ready-to-eat bun per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. The bread accompanies both patties; use a double-patty bun or serve the second patty beside it.

### Equipment

- Two air fryers, each with roughly 8×8 inches usable flat space for four patties

- Instant-read thermometer

- Clean board and serving tools

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Preheat both fryers to 380°F. Prepare cucumber, greens, and yogurt mixed with lemon first. Mix turkey, egg, flax, feta, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper just until combined. If the scaled egg amount is half an egg, beat one whole egg and use half by weight, about 0.88 oz.

2. **Cook.** Form patties about 3.53 oz each, 3¼ inches across and ¾ inch thick; allow about two per adult. Oil baskets lightly. In the four-serving batch, put four patties in each only if they fit with gaps; about 8×8 inches of usable flat space per basket is a starting fit check. Do not cram them in.

3. **Finish.** Cook about 14–18 minutes, flipping once halfway, until each patty reaches 165°F. If serving non-keto diners, warm the chosen family bread during cooking. Serve patties with cucumber, greens, and yogurt sauce. A family bun is one double-patty serving, or put one patty in the bun and the other beside it; pita goes alongside the full plate.

### For a shared table

Keep both turkey patties, salad and yogurt sauce on each plate. Offer the existing pita or bun option separately, using a double-patty bun or serving the second patty alongside.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare and form: 10–12 min. Prepare cold sides first; mix lightly and form patties roughly 3.53 oz each, 3¼ inches across and ¾ inch thick.

- Air fry: 14–18 min. Four patties per basket only if gaps remain; flip once halfway, check each for 165°F. Warm one bread choice during cook.

- Serve: 2 min. Two patties per person with cucumber, greens, and yogurt.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Ground flax binds the turkey; feta and lemon yogurt keep a lean patty from tasting flat.

- Ground flax binds; whole flax is not equivalent.

- Do a cold basket fit check before committing to air frying.

If patties do not fit with gaps, bake on half-sheet pans at 425°F for about 18–22 min; check every patty for 165°F. Four-serving base batch can fit on one pan; larger batches may need more pans or rounds. Allow 35–40 min for the base batch.

Known allergens for these plates: egg, milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

- Patties may require the oven fallback in smaller fryers.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

no more than ¾ inch thick</small></th><td rowspan="7" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Roast seasoned chicken at 425°F for about 20–25 minutes until the thickest pieces reach 165°F.</td><td rowspan="16" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Plate chicken beside green beans; roast about 10–15 minutes to tenderness and remove when ready.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.24 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Divide equally between chicken and green beans.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Dried oregano<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Garlic powder<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.02 oz</strong> Lemon zest<small class="trn-state-detail">finely grated · Use finely grated zest.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.06 tsp</strong> Black pepper<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the proportional split described in the method.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.06 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.28 oz</strong> Nutritional yeast<small class="trn-state-detail">flakes · Add after cooking.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, unfolded; no more than ¾ inch thick

- 1 lb Green beans — trimmed

- 0.48 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Divide equally between chicken and green beans.

- ½ tsp Dried oregano

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- ⅛ tsp Black pepper

- 0.04 oz Lemon zest — finely grated. Use finely grated zest.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.28 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Add after cooking.

### Optional side choices (per diner)

- Plain roasted potatoes: 5 oz Baby potatoes — raw, washed; cut into pieces no larger than ¾ inch. Roast separately on a lined tray at 425°F until fork-tender, about 30–40 minutes. Start before the chicken; keep potatoes off the shared chicken-and-beans plates until serving. No added oil is included in this side.

### Equipment

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

- Oven

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Use two half-sheet pans and an instant-read thermometer. Unfold thawed chicken thighs no more than ¾ inch thick, and trim the beans.

2. **Season.** Before handling raw chicken, mix oil, oregano, garlic, lemon zest and pepper in a clean bowl. Divide the mix and salt equally between chicken and beans, using separate bowls and tools.

3. **Roast.** Roast chicken on its own pan for about 20–25 minutes to 165°F. After the first 10 minutes, add the beans on their separate pan and swap racks. Beans need about 10–15 minutes to become tender. Remove each component when ready.

4. **Serve.** Finish with lemon juice and sprinkle nutritional yeast over the beans. Optional potatoes cook separately and can extend elapsed time.

### For a shared table

Serve lemon chicken and green beans to everyone. Roast the optional potatoes on their own tray and add them only to the plates that request them.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare: 10 min. Season chicken and beans separately.

- Roast: 20–25 min. Add beans after 10 minutes; check chicken reaches 165°F.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Lemon, garlic and oregano season the chicken and green beans. Delaying the beans preserves their texture; lemon juice and nutritional yeast finish the meal after roasting.

- Spread the full bean portion in a single layer on its own pan.

- Keep the chicken pan and raw-chicken tools separate from the beans.

- Optional plain potatoes roast on a separate tray; begin them earlier and check they are fork-tender.

Use additional oven batches if either pan cannot hold the food in a single layer; allow more elapsed time.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Calories: 282 kcal; protein: 36.6 g; fat: 10.7 g; total carbs: 9.6 g; fiber: 3.7 g; net carbs: 5.9 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Optional side nutrition is separate from the base meal. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber − documented erythritol. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: none listed; check every product label. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Pan capacity, thigh thickness and oven performance can change timing; cooking endpoints control.

- Optional potatoes roast separately, without added oil in the modeled side, and can need 30–40 minutes before serving.

- This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested. Check packaged ingredients for additional allergens.

- Keto quantities and sauce balance are editorial adaptations using the recorded ingredient profiles; they have not been kitchen-tested. Brand composition can differ.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

Pan-fried turkey-feta patties with cucumber salad and lemon yogurt.

Turn each batch once; cook every patty to 165°F.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb 93%-lean ground turkey — raw

- 1 count Large egg — as purchased. For fractional eggs, beat whole eggs and weigh 1.76 oz per large-egg portion; half an egg is about 0.88 oz.

- 0.49 oz Ground flaxseed — ground, not whole. Ground seed acts as a binder; whole seeds are not equivalent.

- 1.76 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

- 1 tsp Dried oregano

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- ¼ tsp Black pepper

- 0.16 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Divide among batches.

- 10.58 oz Cucumber — diced

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat

- 4.23 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 3.53 oz.

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

### Optional side choices (per diner)

- Pita: 2.12 oz Pita — ready to eat; warm briefly. One ready-to-eat 2.12 oz pita per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. Serve pita alongside both patties and salad.

- Bun: 1.59 oz Bun — ready to eat; warm briefly. One 1.59 oz ready-to-eat bun per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. The bread accompanies both patties; use a double-patty bun or serve the second patty beside it.

### Equipment

- Stovetop and 12-inch nonstick frying pan

- Instant-read thermometer

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Mix yogurt with lemon. Prepare cucumber and greens. Mix turkey, egg, flax, feta and seasoning just until combined. Form about two patties per serving about 3.53 oz each, 3¼ inches across and ¾ inch thick.

2. **Pan-fry.** Heat a 12-inch nonstick frying pan over medium heat. Divide the oil among batches. Add oil and up to four patties at a time. Cook 5–6 minutes per side, until every patty reaches 165°F. Repeat until all patties are cooked.

3. **Serve.** Serve two patties per person with cucumber, greens and lemon yogurt. Serve the selected bread alongside.

### For a shared table

Serve two pan-fried patties per person with cucumber, greens and lemon yogurt. Offer the existing pita or bun option only to non-keto diners, retaining both patties in their portion.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare: 10–12 min. Mix sauce and form patties.

- Pan-fry two batches: 20–24 min. Turn once per batch and check each patty for 165°F.

- Serve: 2 min. Plate two patties with salad and yogurt.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Ground flax binds the turkey; feta and lemon yogurt keep a lean patty from tasting flat.

- Mix turkey lightly to keep patties tender.

- Use a nonstick pan and divide the measured oil between batches.

### Nutrition per serving

per serving (1/4 of prepared batch)

Fat estimate: Ingredient total fat observations at measured edible weights; no calorie residual inference.

Known allergens for these plates: egg, milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

3. **Serve.** Divide among serving glasses and serve chilled.

### For a shared table

Blend the strawberry, hemp and unsweetened yogurt base, then pour the keto glasses first. Add banana or oats only to the remaining non-keto smoothie and blend again.

### Attention timeline

- Blend: 2 min. Blend in two batches.

Greek yogurt supplies a creamy, tangy base; strawberries add fruit flavor and hemp hearts give body without avocado.

Cooked shredded chicken in a green-chili cheese sauce.

Stir the sauce until smooth, then cover and reheat cooked chicken to 165°F.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

### Ingredients

- ⅔ tbsp Butter

- ⅔ tbsp Minced garlic

- ⅔ count Jalapeño — seeded and chopped. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ⅔ cup Unsweetened almond milk

- ⅙ cup Heavy cream

- 2 oz Cream cheese

- 2.67 oz Canned green chilis — undrained. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- ⅔ tsp Chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.05 oz Ground cumin

- ⅓ tsp Onion powder

- ⅔ cup Shredded cheddar for the sauce

- 1.03 lb Shredded chicken — fully cooked

- ⅓ cup Shredded cheddar for topping

### Equipment

- Stovetop and large lidded skillet

- Whisk and spoon

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Start the sauce.** Set a large skillet over medium heat. Melt the butter, then stir in the minced garlic and seeded jalapeño for about 30 seconds.

2. **Melt the cheeses.** Whisk in almond milk, cream, cream cheese, undrained chilis, chili powder, cumin, onion powder and the sauce portion of cheddar. Keep stirring until the sauce is smooth.

3. **Heat the chicken.** Fold in the fully cooked chicken. Scatter the topping cheddar over it, cover, and turn the heat to low. Simmer for about 10 minutes; confirm the chicken reaches 165°F in several places before serving.

### For a shared table

Serve the green chili chicken as written, with cooked rice or warmed tortillas in separate dishes. Spoon the chicken onto each plate before adding that diner's starch.

### Attention timeline

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Green chilis, cumin and jalapeño season the creamy cheddar sauce.

- Keep the two cheddar portions separate until topping.

### Ingredients

- 8 count Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw

- 4.23 oz G Hughes Sugar Free Honey Mustard

- 1 lb asparagus — tough ends removed

- ½ cup sliced bell pepper

- ¼ cup sliced red onion

- 1 tbsp butter

- 2 tsp minced garlic

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Arrange.** Put chicken at one end of the sheet and season it. Coat with half the honey mustard.

2. **Vegetables.** Arrange the asparagus, pepper and onion at the other end. Mix butter with garlic, drizzle over the vegetables and season to taste.

3. **Roast.** Bake 20–25 minutes, until chicken reaches 165°F internally.

4. **Glaze.** Brush chicken with the remaining mustard. Broil 2–3 minutes, watching the glaze closely.

### For a shared table

Keep the sugar-free honey-mustard chicken and asparagus for everyone. Roast potatoes on a separate tray and offer them only to non-keto diners.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Chicken — raw; cut into chunks

- 0.07 oz cumin

- 1 tsp chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ tsp garlic powder

- ½ tsp onion powder

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp butter

- 1 cup bell pepper — cut into small pieces

- ½ cup onion — cut into small pieces

- 2 count jalapeños — seeded and diced. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- ⅓ cup chicken broth

- 2 oz cream cheese

- 1 cup cheddar — divided

- 1 tbsp Olive oil or 0.04 oz Olive-oil cooking spray. This measured amount is an upper limit, not a mandatory minimum.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Season.** Mix cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken in this blend.

2. **Brown.** Warm a large skillet over medium heat with the source method's spray or oil. Sear chicken 2–3 minutes per side. Add peppers, onion and jalapeños, then cook about 5 minutes, until the vegetables begin softening. Transfer everything to a plate.

3. **Sauce.** Over medium-low heat, melt the listed butter into cream, broth, cream cheese and half the cheddar; stir until thickened.

4. **Finish.** Return the chicken and vegetables, scatter the remaining cheddar on top and cover. Simmer on low for 6–8 minutes, checking the chicken reaches 165°F.

### For a shared table

Serve the cheesy chicken and peppers as a bowl. Offer warmed tortillas alongside, keeping them out of the shared skillet.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb small chicken breast

- 0.07 oz cumin

- ½ tsp chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ tsp garlic powder

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp butter

- ½ cup chopped onion

- 2 count jalapenos — seeded and diced. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 1 tsp minced garlic

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- ⅓ cup chicken broth

- 2 oz cream cheese

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese — divided

- 1 tbsp Olive oil or 0.04 oz Olive-oil cooking spray. This measured amount is an upper limit, not a mandatory minimum.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Season.** Combine the spices and coat both faces of each chicken breast.

2. **Sear.** Warm the skillet over medium with the source spray or oil. Brown the chicken 2–3 minutes per side, then transfer it to a plate.

3. **Sauce.** Melt the butter in the pan; sauté onion, jalapeños and garlic for 3–4 minutes. Lower the heat, pour in cream and broth, and stir in cream cheese until smooth. Melt half the cheddar into the sauce.

4. **Finish.** Return chicken, cover it with the remaining cheddar, then put on the lid. Simmer gently for 6–8 minutes until the chicken is cooked.

### For a shared table

Plate the jalapeno chicken with its measured cheese sauce. Put cooked rice in a separate serving bowl so each non-keto diner can add it to their own plate.

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp butter

- 1 lb chicken breast — cut into cubes

- 1 tsp garlic powder

- 1 tsp onion powder

- ½ tsp paprika

- ¼ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 1 lb broccoli florets

- 1 tbsp butter

- 1 tsp garlic

- 1 cup unsweetened almond milk

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- 3 oz cream cheese

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese

- ½ cup shredded cheddar cheese

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Warm the skillet over medium. Cook cubed chicken in the first butter portion with the dry spices for 5–6 minutes, browning all faces. Set chicken aside.

2. **Cheese sauce.** In the same pan, heat the second butter portion, garlic, almond milk, heavy cream, cream cheese and sauce cheddar. Whisk as the cream cheese melts.

3. **Bake.** Fold chicken and broccoli into the sauce. Add topping cheddar and bake 20–25 minutes. Wait 10 minutes before serving so the sauce can thicken.

### For a shared table

Keep the chicken, broccoli and cheese sauce together as written. Offer baked potatoes separately, with the casserole spooned onto the non-keto diner's potato only after plating.

### Ingredients

- ¼ cup gluten free soy sauce

- 1 tbsp Mizkan unseasoned rice vinegar

- 0.85 oz brown sugar swerve — or other keto friendly sweetener

- 2 tbsp sesame oil

- 2 tsp minced garlic

- 1 tbsp Olive oil or 1 tbsp Sesame oil

- 1.5 lb chicken — thinly sliced

- 1 count medium size zucchini — sliced

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 2 tbsp cashews — chopped

- 2 tbsp green onions — chopped

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

### Ingredients

- 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts — pounded to an even thickness

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 1 tbsp butter

- 2 tbsp butter — divided

- 1 tsp minced garlic

- 8 oz Mushrooms — thinly sliced

- ½ cup white cooking wine or ½ cup Chicken broth — or chicken broth

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- 2 slice Swiss cheese — halved

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Sear.** Coat chicken with Italian seasoning and salt and pepper. Melt the first butter portion in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Sear chicken 3–4 minutes on each face, then reserve it; it will finish cooking later.

2. **Mushrooms.** Use half the divided butter portion to cook garlic and mushrooms with wine or broth. Simmer until nearly all the liquid evaporates.

3. **Finish.** Stir in the rest of the divided butter and the cream. Return chicken and place halved Swiss slices over it. Cover and simmer for 6–8 minutes until the chicken is cooked.

### For a shared table

Plate the mushroom chicken with its Swiss and cream sauce. Offer separately cooked egg noodles for other diners, keeping them out of the shared sauce pan.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb thin cut chicken breasts

- 1 tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp unsalted butter

- 1 cup chicken bone broth or 1 cup Chicken stock — or chicken stock

- 4 clove garlic — minced

- 15.1 oz cauliflower — rice or chopped small

- 1 tbsp fresh thyme

- 2 tbsp heavy cream

- 1 tbsp lemon juice

- 1 tsp lemon zest

- 0.07 oz Fresh thyme — garnish, optional

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Season chicken with salt and pepper. Brown it in butter over medium-high heat for 3–5 minutes, turn, then cook 2–4 minutes more to an internal 165°F. Transfer to a plate and tent with foil.

2. **Cauliflower.** Pour broth into the skillet and add garlic and cauliflower. Loosen the browned residue from the pan and simmer 4–5 minutes until cauliflower is just tender.

3. **Finish.** Take the skillet off the heat. Stir in thyme, cream, lemon juice and zest. Return chicken and add optional thyme garnish.

### For a shared table

Keep the chicken and measured cauliflower in the shared lemon sauce. Offer separately cooked rice for other diners to add to their own plates.

### Ingredients

- ⅔ cup Plain whole-milk Greek yogurt

- 0.35 oz Ginger paste

- 2 clove Garlic, minced

- ⅔ tsp Morton coarse kosher salt

- ⅓ tsp Black pepper

- 1.33 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs cut into bite size chunks

- 1 ⅓ tbsp avocado oil

- ⅔ tsp Morton coarse kosher salt

- 2 ⅔ clove Garlic, minced

- 0.71 oz Ginger paste

- 0.09 oz Garam Masala

- 1 ⅓ tsp Smoked paprika

- 5.33 oz Tomato sauce

- 1 ⅓ tbsp Tomato paste

- ⅓ cup Heavy cream

- 2 tbsp Butter

- 0.28 oz Fresh cilantro for garnish

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Marinate.** Stir yogurt, marinade ginger, marinade garlic, first salt portion and pepper together. Coat chicken and refrigerate for 1 hour.

2. **Cook.** Heat the listed avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken through to 165°F, about 8 minutes. Pour off liquid released by the chicken and marinade so the sauce stays thick.

3. **Sauce.** Stir in the remaining garlic, ginger and salt, plus garam masala and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute. Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, cream and butter; cook a few minutes until thickened.

4. **Serve.** Add the optional cilantro garnish. Cauliflower rice is a serving suggestion rather than a measured part of this recipe.

### For a shared table

Serve the butter chicken sauce as written. Offer cooked basmati rice and naan separately for non-keto diners; any cauliflower-rice accompaniment also needs its own measured serving if included in the keto meal.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs

- 2 count large bell peppers

- 1 lb zucchini

- 2 tbsp olive oil

- 1 lemon Lemon juice

- 2 tbsp Red wine vinegar

- 1 tsp Fine sea salt — fine grains

- ½ tbsp dried oregano

- 1 tsp dried dill

- 1 tsp garlic powder

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Marinate.** Whisk oil, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, oregano, dill and garlic powder together. Coat chicken with half this marinade and refrigerate for 20 minutes or overnight. Keep the other half separate for vegetables.

2. **Arrange.** Place marinated chicken in the middle of the sheet. Put vegetables around it and toss them with the reserved marinade.

3. **Bake.** Roast at 450°F for 25 minutes. Verify chicken reaches 165°F in its thickest part; return to the oven if needed. The source also says to check after 3 minutes, which conflicts with its stated bake time.

### For a shared table

Keep the Greek chicken, peppers and zucchini on the shared tray. Offer warm pita separately so non-keto diners can build wraps at their plates.

bring Marsala to boil and reduce 3–4 min; add broth/cream/spices, bring to boil, lower heat and cover; simmer about 10 min, stirring occasionally until thickened.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 cup</strong> sliced mushrooms<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ cup</strong> Marsala wine<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ cup</strong> chicken broth<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 cup</strong> heavy whipping cream<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 tsp</strong> ground mustard<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 tsp</strong> garlic powder<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.28 oz</strong> Chopped Parsley for garnish<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Boneless skinless chicken breasts — raw; slice horizontally into thin fillets

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 2 tbsp olive oil

- 2 tbsp butter

- 2 cup sliced mushrooms

- ½ cup Marsala wine

- ½ cup chicken broth

- 1 cup heavy whipping cream

- 1 tsp ground mustard

- 1 tsp garlic powder

- 0.28 oz Chopped Parsley for garnish

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Season the chicken to taste. Warm half the oil and all the butter in a large skillet over medium. Fry chicken 3–4 minutes on each side until cooked. Keep it on a plate under foil.

2. **Mushrooms.** Add the remaining oil and sauté mushrooms 2–3 minutes. Pour in Marsala; bring to a boil and reduce for 3–4 minutes.

3. **Sauce.** Stir in broth, cream, mustard and garlic powder. Bring back to a boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.

4. **Finish.** Return chicken for 1–2 minutes to warm it in the sauce. Serve with optional parsley.

### For a shared table

Serve the chicken and mushroom Marsala sauce as written. Offer separately cooked pasta or mashed potatoes for non-keto plates, keeping the starch out of the shared sauce.

for more heat, add gradually to taste.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.1 cup</strong> cilantro<small class="trn-state-detail">chopped</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.23 oz</strong> green onions<small class="trn-state-detail">sliced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.6 cup</strong> Mexican blend cheese<small class="trn-state-detail">divided</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1 lb boneless chicken breast

- 1.6 tbsp olive oil — divided

- 1.6 oz cream cheese — softened

- 0.2 cup sour cream

- 5.6 oz Rotel tomatoes with chilies — canned; measure undrained contents before draining. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 1.2 cup Mexican blend cheese — divided

- 1.2 tbsp taco spice. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 0.6 tbsp dried onion flakes

- 0.4 tsp garlic powder

- 0.04 oz chipotle powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.1 cup cilantro — chopped

- 0.23 oz green onions — sliced

### Equipment

- Oven

- Large skillet

- Baking dish

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Cut chicken into small chunks and coat with taco seasoning and half the olive oil.

2. **Filling.** Blend cream cheese, sour cream, drained tomatoes and half the shredded cheese. Stir in onion flakes, garlic powder, chipotle, cilantro and green onions.

3. **Brown.** Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown chicken in batches without crowding; it can finish cooking in the oven.

4. **Bake.** Mix browned chicken and its juices into the filling. Spread in a shallow casserole dish, cover with remaining cheese and bake around 20 minutes, until bubbling and chicken reaches 165°F.

### For a shared table

Bake the taco chicken casserole as written. Offer tortilla chips or warmed tortillas at the table so non-keto diners can assemble their own portions.

### Ingredients

- 2 count medium zucchini

- 9.88 oz chicken — fully cooked; shredded

- 0.85 oz bacon — cooked and chopped

- ½ cup cottage cheese — blended

- 0.42 oz dry ranch seasoning

- 1 ⅙ cup shredded cheddar — divided

- ⅙ cup green onions — finely chopped

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking dish

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Boats.** Halve zucchini lengthwise. Scoop out centers to make hollows and arrange in a 9-by-13-inch dish.

2. **Fill.** Stir chicken, cottage cheese, ranch seasoning and green onions with half the bacon and three sevenths of the cheddar. Pack into the zucchini hollows and add the remaining cheddar.

3. **Bake.** Bake 20–25 minutes until zucchini yields to a fork. Add the reserved bacon before serving.

### For a shared table

Keep the measured chicken filling in the zucchini boats. Offer garlic bread alongside individual non-keto plates rather than replacing the zucchini in the shared bake.

### Ingredients

- 4 count chicken breast — small to medium size

- 3 oz cream cheese — softened

- 2 tbsp mayonnaise

- ¾ cup Gruyere cheese — shredded

- 2 tsp minced garlic

- 12 spear Asparagus spears — woody ends removed

- 0.16 oz Italian seasoning

- 0.04 oz garlic salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp butter

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

- Toothpicks

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Fill.** Mix cream cheese, mayonnaise, Gruyere and minced garlic. Butterfly each chicken breast without separating the halves. Fill with cheese mixture and asparagus, fold shut and fasten with toothpicks.

2. **Season.** Mix Italian seasoning, garlic salt and pepper, then coat chicken exteriors.

3. **Cook.** Melt butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium. Sear chicken 2–3 minutes per side. Transfer to the oven for about 20 minutes, until cooked through. Rest at least 5 minutes before slicing.

### For a shared table

Keep the cheese-and-asparagus filling inside every chicken breast. Offer roasted potatoes from a separate tray for non-keto plates.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Boneless skinless chicken breasts — raw

- ½ count small green bell pepper — finely chopped

- ½ count small onion — finely chopped

- ½ count jalapeño — seeded and finely chopped. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 5 oz Tomatoes with green chilies — canned; undrained. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 16 fl oz Chicken broth

- 2 oz Diced green chilies — canned. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 0.5 oz Taco seasoning — dry mix. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 4 oz room temp cream cheese — cut into small pieces

- ⅛ cup cream

- ¾ cup shredded cheddar cheese

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

### Equipment

- Lidded saucepan or Dutch oven

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Aromatics.** Heat the unspecified cooking oil over medium in a pot. Sauté onion, bell pepper and jalapeño until softened.

2. **Simmer.** Add chicken, undrained tomatoes, green chilies, taco mix and broth. Cover and simmer 20–25 minutes, adjusting heat as needed.

3. **Cream.** Remove chicken and shred it. While it is out, whisk cream cheese, cream and cheddar into the soup until the cream cheese melts.

4. **Finish.** Return shredded chicken, stir and serve.

### For a shared table

Keep the enchilada soup base as written. Offer cooked rice and tortilla strips separately, adding them only to individual non-keto bowls.

### Ingredients

- 4 count Chicken breasts — raw

- 8 slice Bacon — raw. Use fewer bacon slices for small breasts.

- 0.32 oz Cajun seasoning. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 0.07 oz Cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- 1 cup Tomatoes — chopped

- 1 cup Avocado — chopped

- 1 tbsp Green onions or 1 tbsp Cilantro — chopped

- 1 tsp Lime juice. Add more to taste.

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Wrap.** Mix Cajun seasoning, cumin and garlic powder; rub both sides of chicken. Gently stretch the bacon without tearing, then wrap around the chicken. The original ingredient list uses twice as many bacon slices as chicken breasts; small breasts may need less.

2. **Cook.** Sear wrapped chicken in a skillet over medium for 2–3 minutes per side. Bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes, until chicken reaches 165°F.

3. **Salsa.** Rest chicken at least 5 minutes. Meanwhile mix tomatoes, avocado, green onions or cilantro, lime juice and salt and pepper. Serve salsa with the chicken.

### For a shared table

Serve the bacon-wrapped chicken with its measured avocado salsa. Offer cooked rice separately, keeping salsa and chicken portions intact on every plate.
