### Ingredients

- 4 count small chicken breast

- ¾ cup shredded cheddar cheese

- 3 oz cream cheese — softened

- ¼ cup Fresh jalapeño — seeded and chopped. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.95 oz Bacon — cooked and chopped

- 0.21 oz cajun seasoning — or your favorite all purpose seasoning. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking dish

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

- Toothpicks

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Filling.** Mix jalapeño, cheddar, bacon and cream cheese.

2. **Stuff.** Open each breast with a lengthwise butterfly cut, keeping one edge attached. Spread filling inside, close and secure with a toothpick. Season the outsides with Cajun seasoning.

3. **Bake.** Place in a greased baking dish and bake 25–30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.

### For a shared table

Keep the jalapeno, bacon and cheese filling inside the chicken. Offer mashed potatoes separately for non-keto plates.

### Ingredients

- 1 count Whole chicken — raw; remove innards. One whole 4 lb–5 lb bird per four-portion batch; roast intact, then divide the cooked meat. Larger servings require additional whole birds and oven space.

- 1.41 oz Celery — trimmed, chopped

- 2.47 oz Onion — chopped

- 2.05 oz Lemon wedges — wedges

- 0.14 oz Fresh parsley — fresh

- 2 tbsp softened butter

- 2 tsp tomato paste

- 2 clove Garlic — minced

- 1 tbsp paprika

- 2 tsp thyme

- 1 ½ tsp onion powder

- 1 ½ tsp garlic powder

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp Extra virgin olive oil

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking dish

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

- Roasting pan or cast-iron skillet

- Foil

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Rub.** Combine paprika, thyme, onion powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper to prepare the spice rub. Reserve one ninth for the butter mixture and keep the remainder for the exterior.

2. **Prepare bird.** Fill the cavity with the source-suggested vegetables, herbs and citrus. Mix softened butter, minced garlic, tomato paste and the reserved rub. Ease this mixture beneath the skin.

3. **Season.** Coat the skin with the unspecified olive oil and season generously with remaining rub; extra rub may be left over. Tie legs and wings if desired, and place breast-up in a roasting pan or cast-iron skillet.

4. **Roast.** Roast 45 minutes at 425°F. Reduce to 400°F, tent loosely with foil if browning too quickly, and roast 20–30 minutes longer, until the thickest part reaches 165°F.

### For a shared table

Carve and portion the roast chicken as written. Roast potatoes in a separate pan and serve them only on the plates that want them.

### Ingredients

- ⅔ tbsp butter

- ⅔ tbsp minced garlic

- ⅓ cup jalapeño — seeded and chopped. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ⅔ cup unsweetened almond milk

- ⅙ cup heavy cream

- 2 oz cream cheese

- ⅔ tsp chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.05 oz cumin

- ⅓ tsp onion powder

- ⅔ cup shredded cheddar cheese

- 1.03 lb shredded chicken — fully cooked; shredded

- ⅓ cup shredded cheddar cheese — for topping

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Aromatics.** Melt butter in a large skillet over medium. Sauté garlic and jalapeño for at least 1 minute.

2. **Sauce.** Pour in almond milk and cream, then add cream cheese, spices and the sauce cheddar portion. Whisk until smooth and melted.

3. **Finish.** Stir chicken into the sauce. Scatter the topping cheddar on the surface, cover and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes.

### For a shared table

Serve the creamy jalapeno chicken as written. Offer warmed tortillas or rolls separately so non-keto diners can assemble their own wraps or sandwiches.

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 2 count chicken breast — chopped into bite sized pieces

- 0.21 oz cajun seasoning — or your favorite all purpose seasoning. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 12 oz smoked sausage — sliced

- 1 tbsp butter

- 2 clove minced garlic

- 4 cup chopped cabbage

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Meat.** Season chicken with Cajun mix. Warm the listed olive oil over medium and brown the chicken. Add smoked sausage and cook until browned with crisp edges; remove the meat to a plate.

2. **Cabbage.** In the same skillet, melt butter and add garlic and cabbage. Fry over medium, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage reaches the texture you prefer.

3. **Finish.** Return chicken and sausage, mix, and adjust salt and pepper to taste.

### For a shared table

Keep the Cajun chicken, sausage and cabbage together in the skillet. Offer cooked rice separately and add it only after individual portions have been served.

reduce heat if browning too quickly.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 count</strong> small onion<small class="trn-state-detail">thinly sliced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 cup</strong> Red bell pepper<small class="trn-state-detail">seeded and thinly sliced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 cup</strong> Green bell pepper<small class="trn-state-detail">seeded and thinly sliced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>8 oz</strong> Mushrooms<small class="trn-state-detail">sliced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>3.99 oz</strong> shredded Provolone cheese<small class="trn-state-detail">or your favorite variety</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 2 tbsp olive oil — divided

- 1 lb Chicken breast or 1 lb Chicken thighs — cut into small strips or chunks

- 1 ½ tsp garlic powder

- 1 tsp onion powder

- 1 tsp paprika

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp black pepper

- 1 count small onion — thinly sliced

- 1 cup Red bell pepper — seeded and thinly sliced

- 1 cup Green bell pepper — seeded and thinly sliced

- 8 oz Mushrooms — sliced

- 3.99 oz shredded Provolone cheese — or your favorite variety

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add chicken and the dry seasonings. Toss with tongs and cook 4–5 minutes until browned. Transfer chicken to a plate.

2. **Vegetables.** Heat the remaining oil in the same skillet. Cook onion, peppers and mushrooms for 7–10 minutes, stirring as needed, until peppers soften. Reduce heat if they brown too quickly.

3. **Finish.** Return chicken and cook another 2–3 minutes until cooked through. Lower heat, scatter provolone on top and cover for 2–3 minutes until melted.

### For a shared table

Serve the cheesy chicken, peppers and mushrooms in bowls. Offer hoagie rolls separately so non-keto diners can fill their own sandwiches without adding bread to the skillet.

optional microwave 10–20 sec.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 tbsp</strong> water<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 tbsp</strong> Mizkan unseasoned rice vinegar<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 tbsp</strong> sesame oil<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.42 oz</strong> Swerve brown sugar substitute or <strong>0.42 oz</strong> Brown monkfruit sweetener<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 tbsp</strong> peanut butter<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.06 oz</strong> Green onions<small class="trn-state-detail">sliced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.99 oz</strong> Almonds or <strong>0.99 oz</strong> Peanuts<small class="trn-state-detail">crushed</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2.82 oz</strong> Lettuce leaves<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 1 lb chicken — cut into small pieces

- 1 count green bell pepper — seeded and chopped

- 1 tbsp minced garlic

- ¼ cup chicken broth or ¼ cup Water or ¼ cup White wine — water or cooking wine will work also

- 2 tbsp soy sauce

- 2 tbsp water

- 2 tbsp Mizkan unseasoned rice vinegar

- 2 tbsp sesame oil

- 0.42 oz Swerve brown sugar substitute or 0.42 oz Brown monkfruit sweetener

- 2 tbsp peanut butter

- 1.06 oz Green onions — sliced

- 0.99 oz Almonds or 0.99 oz Peanuts — crushed

- 2.82 oz Lettuce leaves

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Warm oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Cook chicken until it starts browning. Add pepper and garlic and cook, stirring, until chicken is cooked and pepper is tender.

2. **Deglaze.** Reduce heat to medium-low. Pour in broth and scrape the browned residue from the skillet.

3. **Sauce.** Whisk soy sauce, water, vinegar, sesame oil, sweetener and peanut butter together. If needed, warm the mixture in a microwave for 10–20 seconds to make whisking easier.

4. **Finish.** Stir sauce into chicken and peppers. Simmer over medium-low for 5–6 minutes until thickened. Spoon into lettuce and add optional onions and chopped almonds or peanuts.

### For a shared table

Set out the chicken filling, lettuce leaves, measured almonds and green onions separately. Keto diners use the lettuce wraps; other diners can spoon their filling over separately cooked rice.

### Ingredients

- 10.67 oz Ground beef or 10.67 oz Ground turkey — raw; brown and drain in method

- ⅔ count small onion — diced

- 2 cup Cabbage — chopped into medium chunks

- 6.67 oz Tomatoes with green chilies — canned; undrained. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 5.33 oz Tomato sauce — canned

- ⅔ tsp chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ⅔ tsp garlic powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 2.66 oz shredded cheese — cheddar or colby jack is our favorite

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Brown.** Brown beef or turkey in a skillet over medium, then drain excess fat. Add onion and cook 3–5 minutes.

2. **Simmer.** Stir in cabbage, undrained tomatoes, tomato sauce, chili powder, garlic powder and salt and pepper. Cover and cook over medium for 15–18 minutes, stirring occasionally.

3. **Top.** Scatter shredded cheese over the finished casserole.

### For a shared table

Keep the beef, cabbage and tomato casserole as written. Offer cooked rice separately and add it only to individual non-keto bowls.

drain excess; stir in sauce ingredients until cream cheese melts.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ cup</strong> chopped onion<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 tbsp</strong> tomato paste<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 tsp</strong> mustard<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 oz</strong> cream cheese<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ cup</strong> Chicken broth or <strong>½ cup</strong> Beef broth<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> onion powder<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> garlic powder<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> salt<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> pepper<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 cup</strong> shredded cheddar cheese<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 4 slice bacon — chopped into small pieces

- 1 lb Ground beef or 1 lb Ground turkey

- ½ cup chopped onion

- 2 tbsp tomato paste

- 1 tsp mustard

- 2 oz cream cheese

- ½ cup Chicken broth or ½ cup Beef broth

- ½ tsp onion powder

- ½ tsp garlic powder

- ¼ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Bacon.** Lightly grease the skillet and cook bacon over medium until crisp. Transfer it to a plate, reserving only the source-specified portion of grease in the pan.

2. **Meat.** Brown ground meat and onion in the retained bacon fat. Drain excess fat.

3. **Sauce.** Add tomato paste, mustard, cream cheese, broth and dry seasonings. Stir until cream cheese melts and the sauce comes together.

4. **Finish.** Turn heat to low. Add the cooked bacon and cheddar on top, cover and cook for 5–7 minutes until cheese melts.

### For a shared table

Serve the cheeseburger skillet as written. Offer buns and fries separately so non-keto diners can assemble their own plates without mixing bread into the shared skillet.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Steak — sirloin, ribeye or preferred cut

- 8.47 oz Steak marinade — prepared

- 8 count large eggs

- 8 tbsp butter — sliced in half

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Marinate.** Coat steak with marinade in a shallow dish or bag, adding salt and pepper to taste. Marinate for 10 minutes to 1 hour.

2. **Steak.** Heat a heavy skillet over medium and melt half the butter. Sear steak 1–2 minutes per side or until it reaches your preferred doneness. Transfer it to a plate.

3. **Eggs.** Wipe out the skillet and melt the remaining butter. Crack in the eggs and cook until whites are set with yolks still runny. Serve with steak.

### For a shared table

Serve the steak and eggs as written; put toast or breakfast potatoes in a separate dish for diners who want them.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Flank steak or 1.5 lb Thinly sliced top round steak

- 2.12 oz Steak marinade — prepared

- ½ count red bell pepper — cut into thin strips

- 5.29 oz french style green beans

- ⅓ cup white onion — cut into thin strips

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

- Toothpicks

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Coat steak with the prepared marinade in a bag and refrigerate at least 30 minutes. Cut into strips large enough to wrap the vegetables.

2. **Roll.** Put some pepper strips, green beans and onion onto each steak strip. Wrap tightly and fasten with toothpicks.

3. **Sear and bake.** Grease a skillet with spray or a little oil and heat over medium. Sear rolls about 1 minute, rotating to brown every side. Transfer to a baking sheet and bake 10–15 minutes.

### For a shared table

Keep the steak rolls filled with the listed vegetables. Offer cooked rice separately so each diner can add it to their own plate.

### Ingredients

- 0.79 oz Avocado oil

- 0.71 oz White onion — finely chopped

- 0.14 oz Garlic — minced

- 1.2 lb fat-trimmed beef brisket

- 0.8 tsp ground thyme

- 0.3 tsp salt

- 0.2 tsp black pepper

- 5.18 oz Beef broth

- 0.8 tbsp Apple cider vinegar

- 6.4 oz fresh mushrooms — sliced

- 2.54 oz Sour cream

- 0.85 oz Mayonnaise

- 0.06 oz xanthan gum

### Equipment

- Lidded saucepan or Dutch oven

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Brown.** Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium. Sauté onion and garlic about 3 minutes. Add beef, thyme, salt and pepper. Cook about 8 minutes, stirring to brown all sides.

2. **Simmer.** Lower heat to medium-low and add broth and vinegar. Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes. Stir in mushrooms, cover and simmer another 90 minutes.

3. **Thicken.** Remove from heat and stir in sour cream and mayonnaise. Add xanthan in six equal small additions, mixing between each, until thickened. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

### For a shared table

Serve the beef and mushroom sauce as written. Offer cooked egg noodles separately and add them only to individual non-keto plates.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Ground beef or 1 lb Ground turkey

- ½ count green bell pepper — finely chopped

- ½ count jalapeño — seeded and finely chopped. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 1 clove garlic — minced

- 5 oz Tomatoes with green chilies — canned; undrained. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 7.5 oz Tomato sauce — canned

- 16 fl oz Beef broth

- 3.5 oz Tomato paste — canned

- 1 tbsp chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ tsp Oregano

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 0.04 oz Cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

### Equipment

- Lidded saucepan or Dutch oven

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Brown.** Brown ground meat over medium in a saucepan or Dutch oven. Drain excess fat.

2. **Simmer.** Add vegetables, undrained tomatoes, sauce, broth, paste, all spices and salt and pepper. Stir until the paste is fully blended. Simmer uncovered over low for about 25 minutes to reduce and thicken.

### For a shared table

Keep the chili bean-free. Set out heated beans, rice, and tortilla chips separately for individual bowls.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Ground beef or 1 lb Ground turkey — raw; brown and drain in method

- 1 count jalapeño — seeded and diced. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 3 cup Cabbage — chopped medium chunks

- 9.98 oz Canned diced tomatoes — undrained. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 8 oz Tomato sauce — canned

- 0.35 oz Taco seasoning — dry mix. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Brown.** Brown the raw ground beef in a skillet over medium until it reaches 160°F, then drain fat. Add jalapeño and cook 3–5 minutes.

2. **Simmer.** Stir in cabbage, undrained tomatoes, tomato sauce and taco mix. Cover and cook over medium for 15–18 minutes, stirring occasionally.

3. **Top.** Add shredded cheddar on the finished casserole.

### For a shared table

Serve the taco cabbage skillet as a bowl. Put tortillas or tortilla chips beside it for diners to add to their own portions.

### Ingredients

- 10.67 oz flank steak

- 5.31 oz bell peppers of any color

- 1.32 oz small onion

- 2.67 oz Baby Bella mushrooms — sliced

- ⅔ tbsp Worcestershire

- ⅔ tbsp apple cider vinegar

- ⅔ tbsp minced garlic

- 1.33 oz cream cheese

- ⅓ cup shredded mozzarella

- ⅓ cup shredded parmesan

- ⅔ tsp salt

- ⅙ tsp pepper

- 1 ⅓ tbsp butter

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Vegetables.** Brown mushrooms in a dry cast-iron skillet over medium-high with a little of the measured salt. Add half the butter with onions and peppers, cook until browning starts, and reserve the vegetables.

2. **Steak.** Season steak with the remaining salt and the pepper. Heat the remaining butter in the skillet and sear steak in uncrowded batches for 1–2 minutes per side. Transfer steak out.

3. **Combine.** Lower heat to medium. Stir Worcestershire, vinegar and garlic into the pan to loosen browned residue. Return steak and vegetables, add cream cheese and stir until it melts.

4. **Melt.** Scatter mozzarella and parmesan on top. Cover the skillet until cheese melts. The publisher also permits 3–5 minutes under a broiler, which requires an oven-safe skillet and oven.

### For a shared table

Serve the cheesesteak mixture in bowls for keto diners and spoon it into separate toasted rolls for other diners.

### Ingredients

- 13 oz Smoked sausage — cut into thick slices

- 3 cup Cabbage — chopped

- 1 count green bell pepper — chopped

- 1 count onion — chopped

- 0.04 oz Old Bay seasoning

- 2 tbsp butter — cut into 0.25 oz butter slices

### Equipment

- Grill

- Tongs

- Heavy-duty foil

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Pack.** Divide sausage, cabbage, pepper, onion, seasoning and butter evenly among the foil packets.

2. **Seal.** Bring opposite foil edges together, fold twice to seal, then close the ends. Leave space inside for steam and expansion.

3. **Grill.** Cover grill and cook packets for 12 minutes. Rotate each half a turn and cook another 12 minutes until sausage is hot and vegetables are crisp-tender. Open carefully, stir and serve.

### For a shared table

Keep the sausage and cabbage packets as written. Cook potatoes separately and add them only to plates after the packets are opened.

roughly chopped</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 3 slice bacon — roughly chopped

- 8 oz ground mild Italian sausage

- 0.25 oz Butter

- 0.18 oz Garlic — minced

- ¼ tsp ground sage

- ⅛ tsp black pepper

- 1 ⅜ cup chicken broth

- ⅜ cup Heavy whipping cream

- 0.49 oz Parmesan cheese — shredded

- 8 oz radishes — quartered

- 1 oz Kale — stems removed; roughly chopped

### Equipment

- Lidded saucepan or Dutch oven

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Bacon.** Cook bacon in a large pot over medium for 6–8 minutes until crisp. Reserve on a paper-lined plate and discard excess grease.

2. **Sausage.** In the same pot, brown sausage over medium-high for 6–8 minutes, breaking it apart. Reserve it and discard excess grease without washing the pot.

3. **Soup.** Melt butter over medium, then cook garlic, sage and pepper for about 1 minute. Add broth, cream and parmesan, raise heat to medium-high and bring to a simmer. Add radishes and simmer medium-low for 15–20 minutes until fork-tender.

4. **Finish.** Return sausage, add kale, and simmer 5–10 minutes until wilted. Serve topped with the reserved bacon.

### For a shared table

Keep radishes in the shared soup. Offer cooked potato pieces separately for individual non-keto bowls, with bread on the side.

### Ingredients

- 2 lb Bone-in pork chops — raw; 2 inches thick

- 1 tsp salt

- ½ tsp black pepper

- 2 tbsp ghee

- 2 clove garlic — minced

- 2 tsp fresh rosemary — minced

- 2 tbsp heavy whipping cream

- 1 tbsp unsalted butter

- 1 tbsp avocado oil

- 1 lb green beans — ends trimmed and steamed until fork-tender

- 2 clove garlic — thinly sliced

- ½ cup chicken stock

- ¼ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp black pepper

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

- Second skillet

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chops.** Dry pork and season with its salt and pepper portions. Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high and melt ghee. Sear 4–5 minutes per side. Move skillet to the oven for 8–10 minutes, until pork reaches 145°F. Transfer to a plate under foil.

2. **Gravy.** Put the chop skillet over low. Cook gravy garlic and rosemary in the drippings for 2–4 minutes, stirring constantly. Turn off heat and whisk in cream.

3. **Beans.** Heat a second skillet over medium to medium-high. Melt butter with avocado oil. Add pre-steamed beans, sliced garlic, stock and their salt and pepper portions. Cover for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Uncover and cook about 5 minutes more until the liquid evaporates and beans brown in spots.

4. **Serve.** Plate chops with gravy and green beans.

### For a shared table

Plate the pork chops with their cream gravy and green beans. Offer mashed potatoes from a separate bowl for other diners.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Keto-friendly smoked sausage — sliced

- 9.63 oz broccoli florets

- 1 cup red bell pepper — cut into chunks

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 0.21 oz cajun seasoning. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Arrange.** Spread sliced sausage on the pan. Toss broccoli and pepper chunks with oil and Cajun seasoning, then distribute around the sausage.

2. **Roast.** Bake for 15 minutes. Toss the contents and bake another 10–15 minutes, until vegetables reach the tenderness you prefer.

### For a shared table

Keep the sausage, broccoli, and peppers on the shared sheet pan. Serve cooked rice separately for diners to add at the table.

### Ingredients

- 6.75 oz Smoked sausage — sliced

- ½ tsp minced garlic

- ¼ count small onion — finely chopped

- ½ count orange bell pepper — finely chopped

- ½ count red bell pepper — finely chopped

- 1 cup celery — finely chopped

- 16 fl oz Chicken broth or 16 fl oz Beef broth or 16 fl oz Vegetable broth — beef, chicken or vegetable

- 5 oz Tomatoes with green chilies — canned; undrained. Choose a mild version for less heat or a hot version for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 3 oz cream cheese

- ¾ cup shredded cheddar

### Equipment

- Lidded saucepan or Dutch oven

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Brown.** Brown sausage in a stockpot or Dutch oven over medium. Drain excess grease.

2. **Vegetables.** Add garlic, onion, peppers and celery and cook until softened.

3. **Simmer.** Stir in undrained tomatoes and broth. Cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes.

4. **Cheese.** Just before serving, stir in cream cheese and cheddar until melted.

### For a shared table

Ladle the cheesy sausage soup into bowls and offer bread or crackers separately; keep them out of the shared pot.

### Ingredients

- 1.6 lb broccoli florets

- 14 oz Johnsonville Andouille smoked sausage — sliced. Choose a milder sausage for less heat or a hotter sausage for more heat; keep the measured amount. Brands can change the nutrition estimate.

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Roast.** Spread broccoli and sliced sausage on the sheet. Roast for 15 minutes, then turn and toss them. Bake another 5–10 minutes until broccoli reaches your preferred tenderness.

2. **Finish.** Add cheddar and return to the oven for 1–2 minutes to melt. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

### For a shared table

Serve the sausage, broccoli, and cheddar as written, with cooked rice in a separate bowl for non-keto plates.

Retain rendered fat in two equal portions for onions and cabbage; source original uses one tablespoon at each stage, proportional to batch size.</td><td rowspan="6" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Return reserved crisp bacon and serve.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ count</strong> small onion<small class="trn-state-detail">chopped</small></th><td rowspan="5" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Caramelize onion in first retained fat over medium 7–10 min; add second fat, cabbage and seasonings; fry 10–15 min, stirring occasionally until softened to taste.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>4 cup</strong> cabbage<small class="trn-state-detail">chopped</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> salt<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> pepper<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> paprika<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 4 slice thick cut bacon — chopped

- 4 cup cabbage — chopped

- ½ count small onion — chopped

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp pepper

- ½ tsp paprika

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Bacon.** Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium until crisp. Transfer with a slotted spoon to a paper-lined plate. Keep the source-specified first portion of rendered fat in the pan and reserve the rest.

2. **Onion.** Sauté onion in retained fat over medium for 7–10 minutes until caramelized.

3. **Cabbage.** Add a second equal portion of the reserved bacon fat, then cabbage, salt, pepper and paprika. Cook 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened to taste.

4. **Finish.** Stir the cooked bacon back in and serve immediately.

### For a shared table

Serve the bacon and cabbage as written. Offer mashed potatoes separately for diners who want them.

### Ingredients

- 10.67 oz ground Italian Sausage

- ⅔ count small zucchini sliced

- 1 ⅓ cup spinach — roughly chopped

- 1 cup low carb Marinara

- ⅙ cup beef broth

- 2.67 oz cream cheese — softened

- 0.22 cup sour cream

- 1 ⅓ tbsp green onions — chopped

- 1 ⅓ tsp minced garlic

- 0.02 oz Italian seasoning

- ⅓ cup shredded mozzarella

- ⅔ cup shredded mozzarella

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Sausage.** Brown sausage over medium and drain fat. Add zucchini and spinach and cook 2–3 minutes until spinach starts wilting.

2. **Simmer.** Stir in marinara and broth and simmer 6–8 minutes to reduce liquid.

3. **Cheese layer.** Mix cream cheese, sour cream, green onions, garlic, Italian seasoning and the first mozzarella portion in a bowl. Spread over the sausage mixture and add the topping mozzarella.

4. **Bake.** Bake for 20 minutes. Rest at least 5 minutes before serving.

### For a shared table

Keep the zucchini skillet lasagna noodle-free. Serve garlic bread separately for diners who want a carby accompaniment.

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 1.5 lb Boneless Pork Chops

- ¼ cup gluten free soy sauce

- 0.42 oz Swerve brown sugar substitute or 0.42 oz Brown monkfruit sweetener

- 1 tbsp Mizkan unseasoned rice vinegar

- 3 tbsp sesame oil

- 2 tsp minced ginger

- 2 tsp minced garlic

- 1 tsp sriracha — optional if you prefer spicy dishes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 10.58 oz fresh green beans

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Pork.** Heat oil over medium. Add sliced pork and leave undisturbed for 3–4 minutes to brown. Stir and cook another 3–4 minutes until cooked through.

2. **Sauce.** Whisk soy sauce, sweetener, vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and optional sriracha together.

3. **Finish.** Add beans and sauce to pork, tossing to coat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover and cook for 5–7 minutes until beans are tender.

### For a shared table

Keep the sesame pork and green beans together. Serve cooked rice separately and spoon it only onto non-keto plates.

### Ingredients

- 1 ⅓ tbsp lemon juice

- 2 ⅔ tbsp avocado oil — or your favorite oil

- 1 ⅓ tsp lemon zest — finely chopped

- 2 ⅔ clove garlic — crushed

- 0.02 oz red pepper flakes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ⅔ tsp Fine sea salt — fine grains

- 1 lb large shrimp — shelled and deveined, with tails on

- 1 ⅓ bunch Broccolini — cut into small florets

- ⅔ count lemon — thinly sliced optional

- 1 ⅓ tbsp parsley — chopped

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Coat shrimp.** Whisk lemon juice, avocado oil, zest, crushed garlic, pepper flakes and salt. Toss shrimp in this mixture, lift shrimp onto the sheet and keep the liquid in the bowl.

2. **Vegetables.** Toss broccolini in that remaining liquid, then place beside the shrimp. Add optional lemon slices.

3. **Roast.** Bake for 6–10 minutes until shrimp are pink and opaque; broccolini will be crisp-tender. For softer broccolini, remove shrimp first and roast vegetables a few minutes longer. Scatter parsley and serve.

### For a shared table

Plate the shrimp and broccolini directly for keto diners. Offer cooked orzo separately for other diners.

### Ingredients

- 2 fillet Salmon fillets — raw; cut into skewer-sized pieces

- 1 count large zucchini — sliced

- ½ count red onion — sliced

- ¼ cup Olive oil

- ¼ cup Plain whole-milk Greek yogurt

- 2 tbsp minced garlic

- 0.42 oz brown sugar Monkfruit sweetener

- ½ lemon Lemon juice

- 0.04 oz fresh dill

- 1 tbsp Oregano

- 1 tsp salt

- 1 tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

- 0.04 oz fresh dill

- ¼ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

### Equipment

- Grill

- Tongs

- Skewers

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Marinate.** Cut salmon, zucchini and onion into pieces large enough to stay on skewers. Whisk the marinade oil, yogurt, garlic, sweetener, lemon juice, marinade dill, oregano, salt and pepper. Coat salmon and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

2. **Vegetables.** Toss zucchini and onion with the separate vegetable oil, dill, salt and pepper.

3. **Skewer.** Soak wooden skewers for 10 minutes or lightly grease metal ones. Remove salmon from marinade and thread with vegetables.

4. **Grill.** Grill for 4 minutes per side. Turn using the skewer itself or a zucchini piece rather than grabbing salmon, which can break apart.

### For a shared table

Keep the salmon, zucchini, and onion skewers as written. Offer pita or rice in separate serving dishes.

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 1.5 lb Salmon — individual fillets about 6 oz each

- 1 lb asparagus — woody ends trimmed off

- ½ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp black pepper

- 2 tbsp butter — melted

- ½ tsp fresh lemon zest

- 0.04 oz minced fresh dill

- 0.99 oz fresh lemon wedges

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Roast.** Drizzle the tray with oil, arrange salmon and asparagus, and season with salt and pepper. Bake 12–15 minutes until salmon is opaque and flakes, and asparagus is tender. Transfer to a platter.

2. **Butter.** Mix melted butter with lemon zest and dill. Drizzle over salmon and asparagus and serve with lemon wedges.

### For a shared table

Serve the salmon and asparagus with the listed dill butter. Roast potatoes on a separate tray for diners who want them.

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 1 tbsp minced garlic

- ¼ cup red onion — finely chopped

- 1 count fresh jalapeño — chopped and seeds removed. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 10 oz Cauliflower rice — frozen

- 0.11 oz Lime zest — finely grated zest

- 1 tbsp Lime juice — freshly squeezed

- ¼ cup Cilantro — finely chopped

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 1 tbsp olive oil

- 1 tbsp butter

- 2 tbsp minced garlic

- 1 lb shelled shrimp

- ½ tsp chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.04 oz cumin

- ¼ tsp pepper

- ¼ tsp salt

- 0.07 oz Lime zest — finely grated zest

- 1 lime Lime juice — freshly squeezed

- 3 tbsp butter

- ¼ cup cilantro — finely chopped

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

- Second skillet

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Rice aromatics.** Heat the rice oil over medium and sauté its garlic, red onion and jalapeño for 1–2 minutes. Break up frozen cauliflower rice clumps before adding them.

2. **Rice.** Sauté cauliflower rice for 6–8 minutes, stirring until most steam subsides. Raise heat slightly, stir in its lime zest, lime juice and cilantro, and season to taste.

3. **Shrimp.** In another skillet over medium, heat the shrimp oil and its first butter portion. Sauté shrimp garlic about 30 seconds. Add shrimp with chili powder, cumin, salt and pepper; cook 2–3 minutes until pink.

4. **Finish.** Stir the shrimp lime zest and juice, finishing butter and shrimp cilantro into the skillet. Cook 1–2 minutes until butter melts and the sauce thickens. Serve shrimp over the cauliflower rice.

### For a shared table

Keep the cauliflower rice and shrimp in their separate pans until plating. Offer a separate pot of ordinary rice for non-keto bowls.

### Ingredients

- ⅔ tbsp olive oil

- ⅔ count small onion — chopped

- 2 ⅔ clove garlic — minced

- 1 ⅓ count carrots — chopped

- 1 ⅓ stalk celery — chopped

- 1 ⅓ tbsp tomato paste

- 0.09 oz Old Bay

- ⅔ cup good quality dry white wine — such as Sauvignon blanc

- 21.33 fl oz Seafood stock or 21.33 fl oz Vegetable stock

- ½ cup heavy cream

- 1 ⅓ tbsp butter

- 2 clove garlic

- ⅔ tbsp lemon juice

- 10.67 oz uncooked Lobster claw meat

### Equipment

- Lidded saucepan or Dutch oven

- Mixing bowl

- Immersion blender

- Skillet

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Soup base.** Heat oil in the pot over medium. Sauté the first garlic portion with onion, carrots and celery until soft. Stir in tomato paste, stock, Old Bay and wine, then simmer at least 15 minutes.

2. **Blend.** Blend the soup smooth with an immersion blender. Stir in cream, reduce heat to low and cover.

3. **Lobster.** In a separate skillet, sauté raw lobster in butter with the second garlic portion and lemon juice for 3–4 minutes. Stir lobster and its butter sauce into the soup. Blend again if you prefer a smoother texture.

### For a shared table

Serve the lobster bisque as written and offer crusty bread separately for dipping; keep croutons out of the shared pot.

### Ingredients

- 2 tbsp salted butter — softened

- 1 count jalapeño — seeded and finely diced. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.04 oz lime zest

- 1.5 lb salmon

- ½ tsp garlic powder

- 0.04 oz cumin

- 0.04 oz lime zest

- ¼ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- ¼ tsp Paprika

### Equipment

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Butter.** Mix softened salted butter, finely diced jalapeño and the butter's lime zest portion. Chill until firm while preparing fish.

2. **Rub.** Combine garlic powder, cumin, the rub’s lime zest portion, salt and pepper. Add paprika to taste as an explicit adaptation of the source’s missing-unit quantity.

3. **Cook.** Coat the top of salmon with rub. Bake or grill skin-down at 400°F for 7–10 minutes until it flakes readily. Add the chilled jalapeño butter immediately after cooking and let it melt over the fish.

### For a shared table

Serve the salmon with its measured jalapeno-lime butter. Offer cooked rice separately for other plates.

- 6.42 oz Broccoli florets. .

- ¼ cup soy sauce

- 2 tbsp sesame oil

### Equipment

1. **Sauce.** Whisk soy sauce, sweetener, sesame oil, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger together.

2. **Stir-fry.** Heat olive oil over medium and sauté shrimp and pepper for 3–4 minutes until shrimp are pink.

3. **Finish.** Add broccoli and prepared sauce. Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until broccoli is tender, then serve.

### Ingredients

- 4 fillet Tilapia fillet — thawed

- 1.13 lb asparagus — woody ends removed

- 2 tbsp butter

- 4 tsp minced garlic

- 12 tbsp shredded parmesan cheese

- 4 tbsp mayonnaise

- 4 tsp minced green onion

- 2 tsp lemon juice

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 2.12 oz Lemon slices — sliced

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking dish

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **First bake.** Place asparagus and fish beside each other in the dish. Mix melted butter with garlic and drizzle over asparagus. Season asparagus and fish to taste. Bake for 10 minutes.

2. **Topping.** While they bake, mix parmesan, mayonnaise, green onion and lemon juice. Turn fish over and spread this topping onto it.

3. **Finish.** Bake another 6–10 minutes, until asparagus is tender and fish flakes easily. Serve with optional lemon slices.

### For a shared table

Keep the Parmesan-topped tilapia and asparagus in the shared baking dish. Offer potatoes cooked separately for non-keto plates.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Shrimp — raw; peeled and deveined

- ½ tbsp minced garlic

- ½ tbsp paprika

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

- ¼ tsp onion powder

- ¼ tsp garlic powder

- ¼ tsp salt

- ⅛ tsp Cayenne pepper. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 2 tbsp butter — divided

- ¼ cup heavy cream

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Sauté.** Heat skillet over medium and melt half the butter. Add garlic and shrimp, scatter paprika, Italian seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, red pepper and black pepper over them, and toss to coat.

2. **Sauce.** Cook shrimp for 3–4 minutes until pink and tender. Stir in remaining butter and cream to make a creamy sauce.

### For a shared table

Serve the creamy Cajun shrimp as written. Offer cooked rice separately for non-keto diners to add to their own plates.

wilt spinach</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>⅔ tsp</strong> Oregano<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 ⅓ count</strong> Onion<small class="trn-state-detail">medium, minced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>5 ⅓ clove</strong> Garlic<small class="trn-state-detail">minced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2.82 oz</strong> Sun-dried tomatoes<small class="trn-state-essential">drained from oil and chopped</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>⅔ cup</strong> Chicken broth<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>⅔ cup</strong> Heavy cream<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.44 cup</strong> Grated Parmesan cheese<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 ⅓ cup</strong> Spinach<small class="trn-state-detail">or more if you like</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.22 tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">fine grains</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.11 tsp</strong> Black pepper<small class="trn-state-detail">ground</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 2 ⅔ count Chicken breasts

- 4 tbsp Butter — divided

- 0.44 tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- 0.22 tsp Black pepper — ground

- 1 ⅓ tsp Oregano

- 1 ⅓ count Onion — medium, minced

- 5 ⅓ clove Garlic — minced

- 2.82 oz Sun-dried tomatoes — drained from oil and chopped

- ⅔ cup Chicken broth

- ⅔ cup Heavy cream

- 0.44 cup Grated Parmesan cheese

- 1 ⅓ cup Spinach. or more if you like

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Season the chicken with salt, pepper and half the oregano. Reserve some of the combined salt-and-pepper seasoning for the sauce.

2. **Step 2.** Heat two-thirds of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken about 4 minutes per side, until cooked through, then transfer to a plate.

3. **Step 3.** Add the remaining butter, onion, garlic, tomatoes and remaining oregano. Cook the aromatics, then stir in broth, cream and Parmesan. Simmer 2–3 minutes until smooth; adjust the seasoning.

4. **Step 4.** Wilt the spinach in the sauce. Return the chicken and heat for 2–3 minutes; serve immediately.

### For a shared table

Serve the spinach Parmesan chicken and sauce as written. Offer cooked pasta separately and add it only to individual non-keto portions.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Medium raw shrimp — peeled and deveined

- 1.5 lb Asparagus — rinsed and trimmed

- 3 tbsp Butter

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

- 5 clove Garlic — minced

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

- 2 tsp Onion powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- ¼ cup Vegetable stock

- 1 tbsp Sriracha. or any hot sauce you like For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.02 oz Crushed chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- 0.28 oz Fresh parsley or 0.28 oz Fresh cilantro — for garnish

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Warm olive oil and one-third of the butter over medium heat. Season asparagus with part of the salt and pepper and cook 4–6 minutes until crisp-tender; set aside.

2. **Step 2.** Melt the remaining butter in the same skillet. Season shrimp with the remaining salt and pepper and cook 1–2 minutes on the first side.

3. **Step 3.** Add garlic, Italian seasoning and onion powder; flip shrimp and cook another minute. Add stock and hot sauce, then simmer about 1 minute until shrimp are cooked through and the sauce has reduced slightly.

4. **Step 4.** Return asparagus, add lemon juice and warm 1 minute. Finish with herbs and optional chili flakes.

### For a shared table

Keep the shrimp and asparagus in the shared skillet. Serve cooked rice separately for diners who want it beneath their portion.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Large shrimp — peeled and deveined

- 1 tsp Chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 2 tsp Paprika

- 1 tsp Onion powder

- 0.07 oz Cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- 1 tsp Salt

- ¼ tsp Freshly cracked black pepper

- 1 tbsp Olive oil — divided

- 1 tbsp Unsalted butter — divided

- 1.5 lb Asparagus — rinsed and trimmed

- ¼ cup Vegetable stock

- 1 tbsp Sriracha — optional. we used Sriracha For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 1 tbsp Lemon juice

- 0.02 oz Lemon slices — sliced. Use fewer chili flakes for less heat or more for more heat; adjust the flakes separately from the other garnishes.

- 0.02 oz Red pepper flakes — flakes. Use fewer chili flakes for less heat or more for more heat; adjust the flakes separately from the other garnishes.

- 0.28 oz Fresh parsley — chopped. Use fewer chili flakes for less heat or more for more heat; adjust the flakes separately from the other garnishes.

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Toss shrimp with chili powder, paprika, onion powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt and black pepper.

2. **Step 2.** Heat half the oil and half the butter over medium-high. Sear shrimp 2–3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through; transfer to a plate.

3. **Step 3.** Clean scorched residue if needed. Add remaining oil and butter over medium heat, then stock, lemon juice and optional hot sauce. Simmer briefly to reduce, add asparagus and cook 4–6 minutes until crisp-tender, turning to coat.

4. **Step 4.** Return shrimp and warm 1–2 minutes. Serve with the optional lemon, chili flakes and parsley garnish.

### For a shared table

Plate the blackened shrimp and asparagus as written. Offer cooked rice separately, with hot sauce at the table for individual heat preferences.

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 4 count Chicken thighs — skinless, boneless

- 1.33 lb Green beans — trimmed

- 4 tbsp Butter or 4 tbsp Ghee — divided or. ghee for paleo diet

- 5 ⅓ clove Garlic — minced

- 1 ⅓ tsp Paprika

- 1 ⅓ tsp Onion powder

- 0.22 tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- 0.11 tsp Black pepper — ground

- ⅔ count Lemon — juice. lemon slices for garnish

- ⅔ cup Chicken stock

- 1 ⅓ tbsp Sriracha. we used Sriracha For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.02 oz Crushed red chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ⅔ cup Fresh chopped parsley

- ⅔ cup Water — for microwave steaming

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

- Microwave

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Dry chicken thighs. Mix paprika, onion powder, salt and pepper; coat the chicken.

2. **Step 2.** Place green beans and the measured steaming water in a microwave-safe dish. Microwave 8–10 minutes, leaving beans slightly crisp.

3. **Step 3.** Melt two-thirds of the butter in a cast-iron skillet over medium-low heat. Cook thighs 5–6 minutes per side, lowering heat if needed, until the thickest portion reaches 165°F. Set aside.

4. **Step 4.** Lower heat and melt the remaining butter. Stir in parsley, garlic, hot sauce, optional chili flakes and the green beans; cook 4–5 minutes. Add lemon juice and stock, reducing for a few minutes.

5. **Step 5.** Return chicken to the pan and warm through. Serve with the source lemon garnish if available.

### For a shared table

Serve the chicken and green beans directly on keto plates, with cooked potatoes in a separate dish for other diners.

### Ingredients

- 3 count Chicken breasts — boneless, skinless, cut into bite-sized chunks

- 2 bunch Asparagus — rinsed and trimmed

- ½ cup Butter — divided. ¼ cup for browning the chicken and ¼ cup for the sauce

- 1 tsp Olive oil

- 2 tsp Minced garlic — divided. 1 tsp for the chicken bites and 1 tsp for the asparagus and sauce

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning or 0.04 oz Herbes de Provence

- 1 tbsp Sriracha — optional. we used Sriracha For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ cup Low-sodium chicken broth

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- 1 tbsp Minced parsley

- 0.02 oz Crushed red chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 2.12 oz Slices of lemon for garnish

- 1 tsp Salt

- 1 tsp Fresh cracked black pepper

- 2 tsp Onion powder

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Season the chicken chunks with salt, pepper and onion powder. Blanch trimmed asparagus for 2 minutes, chill in ice water and drain; very thin stalks can skip blanching.

2. **Step 2.** Melt half the butter with olive oil over medium heat. Brown chicken on all sides, working in batches if necessary. Lower heat, add half the garlic and the Italian herbs, and cook 1 minute until fragrant. Transfer chicken to a plate.

3. **Step 3.** Raise heat to medium-high. Add the remaining garlic and broth, simmering until reduced by half. Stir in the remaining butter, lemon juice, optional hot sauce and parsley.

4. **Step 4.** Toss asparagus in the sauce for 2 minutes, then return chicken and heat 1 minute. Serve with optional chili flakes and lemon slices.

### For a shared table

Plate the chicken bites and asparagus with their lemon butter sauce. Offer cooked pasta separately for non-keto plates.

## Creamy Tuscan Salmon Recipe

### Ingredients

- 4 count Salmon fillets

- 2 ⅔ tsp Olive oil

- 2 ⅔ tbsp Butter

- 6 ⅔ clove Garlic — finely diced

- 2.12 oz Yellow onion — small, diced

- 0.44 cup Vegetable broth

- 2.12 oz Jarred sun-dried tomato in oil — drained of oil

- 1 cup Heavy cream

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 4 cup Baby spinach leaves

- ⅔ cup Grated Parmesan

- 1 ⅓ tbsp Fresh parsley — chopped

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Heat olive oil over medium-high. Season salmon with part of the salt and pepper. Sear flesh side first, about 5 minutes per side or until cooked to the source preference; set aside.

2. **Step 2.** Melt butter in the same skillet. Fry garlic about 1 minute; add onion and cook until translucent. Add drained tomatoes for 1–2 minutes, then broth; reduce slightly.

3. **Step 3.** Lower heat and gently simmer cream, seasoning with the remaining salt and pepper. Wilt spinach, stir in Parmesan and simmer 1 minute to melt.

4. **Step 4.** Return salmon, scatter parsley over it and spoon sauce over the portions before serving.

### For a shared table

Serve the Tuscan salmon and spinach directly on keto plates. Offer cooked pasta separately so other diners can spoon their fish and sauce over it.

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Sirloin steak — sliced against the grain

- 2 head Broccoli — cut into florets

- 2 tbsp Olive oil

- 4 clove Garlic — minced

- 3 tbsp Butter or 3 tbsp Ghee

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- ¼ cup Low-sodium beef broth

- ¼ cup Parsley — chopped. Use the parsley in the sauce.

- 0.02 oz Crushed red pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ¼ tsp Fresh cracked black pepper

- 0.07 oz Fresh thyme — for garnish

- ⅓ cup Low-sodium soy sauce or ⅓ cup Big Tree Farms Coconut Aminos. or coconut amino if you’re strictly paleo

- ½ cup Olive oil

- 1 tbsp Sriracha sauce. or any hot chili sauce you like For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Combine soy sauce, marinade olive oil and hot sauce. Add steak strips and refrigerate 30–60 minutes.

2. **Step 2.** Blanch broccoli florets 1–2 minutes, then rinse with cold water. Drain steak while reserving its marinade.

3. **Step 3.** Heat the cooking olive oil and one-third of the butter over medium-high. Sear steak in batches for 1–2 minutes per side until browned; set aside.

4. **Step 4.** Lower to medium and melt remaining butter. Add lemon, garlic, broth and reserved marinade; bring to a full boil before reducing. Add parsley and broccoli, tossing until broccoli is done to preference.

5. **Step 5.** Return steak briefly to warm. Finish with optional chili flakes, black pepper and thyme.

### For a shared table

Keep the steak and broccoli in their boiled-and-reduced marinade sauce. Serve cooked rice separately for individual non-keto portions.

### Ingredients

- 1.25 lb Sirloin steak — cut into small cubes

- 4 count Zucchini or 1.73 lb Packaged zucchini noodles — medium, spiralized

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

- 3 tbsp Butter — divided

- 2 tsp Minced garlic

- ¼ cup Beef broth or ¼ cup Vegetable broth

- 1 tbsp Minced parsley

- 1 tsp Fresh thyme leaves

- 0.03 oz Red chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- ¼ cup Low-sodium soy sauce or ¼ cup Big Tree Farms Coconut Aminos. or coconut amino for paleo and gluten-free

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

- 1 tbsp Sriracha. we used Sriracha For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ¼ tsp Fresh cracked black pepper

- ½ count Lemon — juice

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Mix soy sauce, marinade olive oil, hot sauce, pepper and marinade lemon juice. Coat steak cubes and marinate at least 15–20 minutes.

2. **Step 2.** Heat cooking olive oil over high heat. Drain steak and retain marinade. Sear cubes in a single layer 3–4 minutes, stirring; work in batches.

3. **Step 3.** Add two-thirds of the butter and garlic, tossing 1–2 minutes. Remove steak to a plate.

4. **Step 4.** Add remaining butter, sauce lemon juice, optional flakes, broth and reserved marinade. Bring the marinade to a full boil before reducing for 2–3 minutes.

5. **Step 5.** Add zucchini noodles for 2–3 minutes. Stir in parsley and thyme; reduce watery juices another minute if needed. Return steak and warm 1 minute before serving.

### For a shared table

Keep zucchini noodles in the shared steak dish. Cook pasta separately, then add it only to individual non-keto servings.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Flank steak — sliced against the grain

- 4 count Zucchini — medium

- 2 tbsp Olive oil

- 4 clove Garlic — minced

- 2 tbsp Butter or 2 tbsp Ghee

- 1.76 oz Lemon — juice and zest

- ¼ cup Low-sodium chicken broth

- ¼ cup Chopped parsley

- 0.02 oz Crushed red pepper flakes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- ⅓ cup Low-sodium soy sauce or ⅓ cup Big Tree Farms Coconut Aminos. or coconut amino if you’re strictly paleo

- ¼ cup Lemon juice

- ½ cup Olive oil

- 1 tbsp Sriracha sauce. or any hot chili sauce you like For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Mix marinade soy sauce, lemon juice, olive oil and hot sauce; coat steak strips and refrigerate 30–60 minutes. Spiralize zucchini while it rests.

2. **Step 2.** Heat cooking olive oil over medium-high. Drain steak, reserving marinade, and season with salt and pepper. Sear in one layer 1 minute without stirring. Add garlic and turn for another 1–2 minutes; set aside.

3. **Step 3.** Add butter, whole-lemon juice and zest, chili flakes, broth and reserved marinade. Bring marinade to a full boil before reducing 2–3 minutes.

4. **Step 4.** Add parsley and zucchini noodles; toss 2–3 minutes. Reduce watery juices another minute if needed, return steak and warm 1 minute. Serve immediately.

### For a shared table

Keep the steak with its zucchini noodles as written. Offer cooked pasta separately so diners can add it to their own plates.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Medium raw shrimp — peeled and deveined

- 1.5 lb Broccoli — rinsed and cut into florets

- 3 tbsp Butter

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

- 5 clove Garlic — minced

- 1 tsp Paprika

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

- 2 tsp Onion powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- ¼ cup Vegetable stock

- 1 tbsp Sriracha. or any hot sauce you like For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.02 oz Crushed chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- 0.28 oz Fresh parsley or 0.28 oz Fresh cilantro — for garnish

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Heat olive oil and one-third of the butter over medium. Season broccoli with part of the salt and pepper and cook 4–6 minutes until crisp-tender; set aside.

2. **Step 2.** Add the remaining butter and shrimp, seasoned with the remaining salt and pepper. Cook 1–2 minutes on the first side.

3. **Step 3.** Add garlic, paprika, Italian seasoning and onion powder. Flip and cook 1 minute; add stock and hot sauce and reduce 1 minute, keeping shrimp tender and cooked through.

4. **Step 4.** Return broccoli, squeeze over lemon juice and warm 1–2 minutes. Finish with optional chili flakes and herbs.

### For a shared table

Serve the shrimp and broccoli as written, with cooked rice in a separate bowl for diners who want it.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Shrimp — peeled and deveined

- ⅓ count Red bell pepper — cut into strips

- ⅓ count Green bell pepper — cut into strips

- 1.4 oz Yellow bell pepper — cut into strips

- ⅓ count Yellow onion — medium, sliced

- ⅔ tsp Dried garlic

- 0.13 oz Ancho chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.07 oz Ground cumin

- ⅔ tsp Ground paprika

- 0.02 oz Ground coriander

- 0.22 tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- 0.11 tsp Black pepper — ground

- 2 tbsp Olive oil

- 1 ⅓ tbsp Lime juice or 1 ⅓ tbsp Lemon juice

- 2 tbsp Chopped cilantro

### Equipment

- Oven

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Heat oven to 400°F. Lightly oil a rimmed baking sheet using a small share of the listed oil. Mix the chili powder, cumin, paprika, coriander, salt and pepper.

2. **Step 2.** Arrange pepper strips and sliced onion on the sheet; add shrimp, dried garlic and seasoning. Drizzle the remaining oil and toss, then spread in an even layer.

3. **Step 3.** Roast 8–10 minutes, tossing halfway, until shrimp are cooked through and vegetables tender. For more browning, broil during the last 2 minutes.

4. **Step 4.** Finish with citrus juice and cilantro. The source suggests warm tortillas and other toppings; these are optional accompaniments with no listed amounts.

### For a shared table

Serve the shrimp and peppers in bowls for keto diners. Set out warm tortillas separately so other diners can assemble fajitas.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Cod fillet or 1.5 lb Halibut fillet — medium; cut each fillet into 3 or 4 chunks. or halibut fillet

- 2 bunch Asparagus — rinsed and trimmed

- 1 tsp Olive oil

- 2 tsp Minced garlic

- ½ cup Low-sodium vegetable broth or ½ cup White wine. or white wine

- ½ stick Unsalted butter

- 1 tbsp Sriracha — optional. we used Sriracha For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- 1 tbsp Minced parsley or 1 tbsp Fresh cilantro. or cilantro

- 0.02 oz Crushed red chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 2.12 oz Slices of lemon — for garnish

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Prepare cod portions. Blanch asparagus in boiling water 2–3 minutes, cool in ice water and drain; very thin asparagus can skip this step.

2. **Step 2.** Warm olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low. Cook fish on both sides until golden and cooked through, then set aside.

3. **Step 3.** Over medium heat, add garlic and deglaze with vegetable broth. Simmer, then stir in butter, lemon juice, optional hot sauce and parsley.

4. **Step 4.** Toss asparagus in sauce 2 minutes. Return fish and warm 1 minute. Finish with optional chili flakes and lemon slices.

### For a shared table

Plate the cod and asparagus with their lemon butter sauce. Offer rice separately for non-keto plates.

bring reserved raw-chicken marinade to full boil, then cook 3–4 min until reduced and zucchini tender.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 3 lb Chicken breast

- 2 count Zucchini — medium-sized, diced

- 8 clove Garlic — minced

- 2 tsp Oregano

- 1 tbsp Smoked Paprika

- 0.15 oz Cumin Powder

- ¼ cup Chicken stock

- ¼ cup Lemon juice — more for serving

- ½ tsp Onion Powder

- 0.03 oz Chili Flakes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ¼ cup Olive Oil — for marinade

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 1 tbsp Olive oil for searing — for searing

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Combine smoked paprika, cumin, stock, lemon juice, onion powder, oregano, garlic, chili flakes and the marinade olive oil. Season to taste before adding chicken; coat, cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

2. **Step 2.** Drain chicken and retain marinade. Heat the separate searing olive oil over medium-low. Cook chicken on both sides for about 15 minutes total, until its center reaches 165°F; set aside.

3. **Step 3.** Cook diced zucchini in the same pan 2–3 minutes. Add the reserved marinade, bring it to a full boil, then continue cooking 3–4 minutes until reduced and zucchini are tender.

4. **Step 4.** Slice chicken and serve over zucchini with its sauce.

### For a shared table

Serve sliced asado chicken over its lemon zucchini. Put cooked rice or tortillas in separate dishes for other diners.

### Ingredients

- 3 count Chicken breasts — boneless, skinless, cut into bite-sized chunks

- 4 count Zucchini — medium, rinsed and spiralized

- 4 tbsp Butter — divided

- 2 tsp Minced garlic

- 1 tbsp Sriracha. we used Sriracha For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ¼ cup Low-sodium chicken broth

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- 1 tbsp Minced parsley

- 1 tsp Fresh thyme leaves

- 0.02 oz Crushed red chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 2.12 oz Slices of lemon — for garnish

- 2 tbsp Olive oil

- 1 tbsp Sriracha or 1 tsp Chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 2 tsp Salt

- 1 tsp Fresh cracked black pepper

- 2 tsp Garlic powder

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Coat chicken chunks with marinade olive oil, hot sauce, salt, pepper, garlic powder and Italian herbs. Refrigerate 30–60 minutes; spiralize zucchini meanwhile.

2. **Step 2.** Melt half the butter over medium-low. Brown chicken on all sides, working in batches, and cook through; set aside.

3. **Step 3.** Over medium-high, add remaining butter, lemon juice, sauce hot sauce and broth. Simmer 1–2 minutes.

4. **Step 4.** Add parsley and minced garlic, then toss zucchini noodles in the sauce 2–3 minutes. Reduce watery juices an extra minute if needed. Return chicken and warm 1 minute; garnish with thyme, optional chili flakes and lemon slices.

### For a shared table

Keep the chicken bites with zucchini noodles in the shared skillet. Offer cooked pasta separately for non-keto diners to add after serving.

### Ingredients

- 4 count Cod fillets

- 1 tbsp Lemon juice

- 3 tbsp Butter — melted

- 1 tsp Dried garlic

- 0.05 oz Red chili powder. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.03 oz Red chili pepper flakes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.04 oz Cumin powder

- ⅙ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- 0.08 tsp Black pepper — ground

- ¼ cup Vegetable broth

- 1 count Lemon — sliced

- 2 tbsp Fresh parsley — chopped

- 2 tbsp Olive oil — for searing

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

- Oven

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Preheat oven to 400°F. Mix lemon juice with melted butter. Separately mix dried garlic, chili powder, chili flakes, cumin, salt and pepper.

2. **Step 2.** Dry cod; brush with half the lemon butter and coat with seasoning. Keep the remaining butter mixture separate for finishing.

3. **Step 3.** Heat the olive oil over medium in an oven-safe skillet. Sear cod 1 minute per side, then loosen pan juices with vegetable broth and pour the remaining lemon butter over fish.

4. **Step 4.** Bake about 10 minutes, checking earlier, until fish flakes readily. Use oven mitts to remove skillet; finish with parsley and lemon slices.

### For a shared table

Serve the baked cod with its measured lemon-butter sauce. Offer bread or rice separately for diners who want it.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Raw medium shrimp — peeled and deveined

- 4 count Zucchini — medium

- 1 tbsp Olive oil

- 4 tbsp Butter or 4 tbsp Ghee — softened, divided

- 4 clove Garlic — finely chopped

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

- 0.0035 oz Red pepper flakes. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ count Lemon — juice

- ¼ cup Chicken stock or ¼ cup Vegetable stock or ¼ cup White wine. or white wine

- 1 tsp Sriracha. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- ¼ cup Chopped fresh parsley — for garnish

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Spiralize trimmed zucchini. Heat olive oil with half the butter over medium-high.

2. **Step 2.** Lay shrimp in a single layer and season. Cook 1 minute untouched; add garlic, Italian herbs and chili flakes, then stir and cook another 1–2 minutes. Set shrimp aside.

3. **Step 3.** Add remaining butter, lemon juice, stock and hot sauce. Simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring.

4. **Step 4.** Toss zucchini noodles in the sauce about 2 minutes, reducing excess liquid if needed. Return shrimp and warm 1 minute, then scatter parsley over the dish.

### For a shared table

Keep the shrimp and zucchini noodles together. Cook spaghetti separately and add it only to individual non-keto portions.

cook peppers 2–3 min, garlic 1 min; reduce broth</td><td rowspan="9" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Gently simmer cream and seasoning; melt measured Parmesan 1 min</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>3 clove</strong> Garlic<small class="trn-state-detail">finely diced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.88 oz</strong> Yellow onion<small class="trn-state-detail">small, diced</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>2 count</strong> Red bell peppers<small class="trn-state-detail">chopped into chunks</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>⅓ cup</strong> Low-sodium vegetable broth<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>⅔ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">fine grains</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>⅓ tsp</strong> Black pepper<small class="trn-state-detail">ground</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¾ cup</strong> Heavy cream<small class="trn-state-detail">or less</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ cup</strong> Grated Parmesan<small class="trn-state-detail">optional</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1 tbsp</strong> Fresh parsley<small class="trn-state-detail">chopped</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Large shrimp — peeled and deveined

- 14 oz Fully cooked pork sausage or 14 oz Fully cooked chicken sausage — fully cooked smoked sausage, sliced. Choose fully cooked pork or chicken sausage.

- 0.42 oz Cajun seasoning. Choose a mild blend for less heat or a hot blend for more heat; keep the measured amount.

- 2 tbsp Olive oil

- 1 tbsp Unsalted butter

- 3 clove Garlic — finely diced

- 0.88 oz Yellow onion — small, diced

- 2 count Red bell peppers — chopped into chunks

- ⅓ cup Low-sodium vegetable broth

- ⅔ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ⅓ tsp Black pepper — ground

- ¾ cup Heavy cream. or less

- ½ cup Grated Parmesan — optional

- 1 tbsp Fresh parsley — chopped

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Toss shrimp and sliced fully cooked sausage with Cajun seasoning and olive oil. Cook over medium-high in a large skillet about 5 minutes until shrimp are cooked and sausage is hot, then set aside.

2. **Step 2.** Melt butter in the pan. Soften onion, cook bell peppers 2–3 minutes, then add garlic for about 1 minute. Add broth and reduce slightly.

3. **Step 3.** Lower heat, stir in cream and salt and pepper, and simmer gently. Add measured Parmesan and simmer another minute to melt it.

4. **Step 4.** Return shrimp and sausage, coat with sauce and sprinkle with parsley; serve.

### For a shared table

Serve the creamy shrimp and sausage as written. Offer cooked rice separately for non-keto diners to add to their own bowls.

for more heat, add gradually to taste.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Medium raw shrimp — peeled and deveined

- ¼ cup Unsalted butter — divided

- 0.04 oz Italian seasoning

- 1 tsp Onion powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt — fine grains

- ¼ tsp Black pepper — ground

- 6 tbsp Vegetable stock. One-third to cauliflower and two-thirds to shrimp.

- 1 tbsp Sriracha. or any hot sauce you like For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 1 head Cauliflower — riced

- 0.88 oz White onion — chopped

- 5 clove Garlic — minced

- 2 oz Fresh Parmesan — finely grated

- 1 count Lemon — juice. + zest, if you like

- 0.06 oz Red chili pepper flakes — optional. For less heat, use less; for more heat, add gradually to taste.

- 0.28 oz Fresh parsley — chopped

### Equipment

- Stovetop

- Pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Step 1.** Season shrimp with part of the salt and pepper. Melt half the butter over medium, then cook half the garlic and the onion 1 minute. Stir in riced cauliflower for 1 minute.

2. **Step 2.** Add one-third of the stock, half the parsley and optional lemon zest; cook 1 minute. Add lemon juice and two-thirds of the Parmesan; cook 1 minute until cauliflower is crisp-tender, then set aside.

3. **Step 3.** Melt remaining butter. Add shrimp and cook 1–2 minutes on one side, then add remaining garlic, Italian herbs and onion powder. Flip and cook 1 minute.

4. **Step 4.** Add remaining stock, hot sauce and Parmesan; reduce 1 minute, finishing shrimp without overcooking. Return cauliflower to warm, add remaining parsley and optional flakes, and adjust seasoning.

### For a shared table

Keep the Parmesan cauliflower rice as the shared base. Offer ordinary cooked rice separately and add it only to individual non-keto portions.
